These estimates yield the Gaussian limit by the method of moments. We also study partial sums of the form $\sum_{n<N} F(f(n),f(N-n))$ for a suitable class of bivariate functions $F$ when $f$ is a Steinhaus random multiplicative function, and prove analogous results in special cases in the Rademacher setting. These results can be viewed as random analogues of the Goldbach-type problems considered by Mangerel.

papers.title: Designing Collaborative Virtual Environments for Software Engineering Education
papers.abstract: Collaborative virtual environments offer opportunities to make software models available for shared inspection, but educational design and usability need to be examined separately from claims of learning effectiveness. This article presents MetaSEE, an approach connecting requirements guidance, a Web XR feature model, a reusable UML component, and a browser-based multiuser platform. We synthesize documented formative evaluations of the framework (16 participations), feature model (15), UML component (9), and platform (14). These counts represent evaluation participations; the same 12 developers took part in the first two evaluations. The principal platform study involved six teachers working individually and eight students working in four pairs through desktop or notebook computers, keyboard, and mouse. The documentary synthesis traces educational intentions to implemented features and reported difficulties. Participants identified potential value in shared modeling and simulation, alongside navigation, interaction, visualization, and distraction concerns. A numerical audit reconstructs a student System Usability Scale mean of 67.50 from published item frequencies, conflicting with the reported 79.38; an incomplete teacher item distribution prevents recovery of that group's overall mean. The contribution is a traceable account of educational design and formative limitations, with practical implications for onboarding, model readability, collaboration, and evaluation reporting. The evidence supports bounded feasibility and perceived usefulness, without establishing learning gains, sustained engagement, or adoption.

papers.title: Rational layers in the low temperature expansion of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: A low-temperature expansion orders Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can occur at the same order. We instead organize the zero-field simple-cubic model by the excess above the minimum wall area compatible with two prescribed spans. We prove that every fixed excess layer, including all logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, has a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1 - x, 1 - y and 1 - x - y. The proof compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations and assigns each unbounded interval to one monotone chain. A finite controller then enforces induced contacts and arbitrary cover-color reuse. We explicitly assemble the complete layers of excess zero through three over all widths, attributing their known geometric constituents to earlier polyomino enumeration. Exact lattice checks corroborate the formulas. A certified low-temperature comparison shows a modest hybrid accuracy gain at one sampling point and higher evaluation cost. The result establishes an exact layer structure; summation over unbounded excess remains a separate problem.

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

papers.title: Rotor-driven piecewise cross polarization of wide quadrupolar lines: bath-contact pumping of vector and tensor order in dynamically polarized solids
papers.abstract: In a dynamically polarized solid with a common nuclear spin temperature, spin-1 $^{14}$N in ammonia sits at $P_N\simeq0.14$ when the protons are at $0.90$, and a deuteron in a proton-rich matrix at $P_D\simeq0.29$. Hartmann--Hahn cross polarization (CP) from the protons could raise either toward $P_H$, but the first-order quadrupole interaction spreads the $^{14}$N line over $5$~MHz at $5$~T, far beyond any single contact bandwidth. We develop the theory of CP into one transition of a quadrupolar spin-1, with slow sample rotation carrying each crystallite through a fixed-frequency contact window. A bath contact is an idempotent map on the populations of the contacted transition, so repeated or continuous contacts accumulate rather than cancel, and the hit-once and parity constraints that force stepped rotation for pulsed inversions do not arise. In the small-reservoir limit the population ratio across the contacted transition becomes $(1+P_H)/(1-P_H)$, giving $\Pzz=+0.88$ in one contact and $\Pzz\to-1.8$ in two from $P_H=0.9$, beyond the unitary bound $[-0.85,+0.65]$. Under continuous rotation, a window at the Pake horn reaches every bond for an axis perpendicular to the field, while a window in the clean pedestal region, needed for a definite sign of tensor order, reaches a fraction $\sin2θ_c=0.943$ at the magic angle $54.74\degree$. Steady-state order is set by the contact rate against rotation-driven cross-branch relaxation, negligible for $^{14}$N. In the cubic limit one contact places the spin-1 at the proton temperature ($\Pzz=+0.85$), but only a resolved quadrupole splitting permits negative tensor order. The limiting resource is the proton spin lock, which must far exceed the $\simeq28$~kHz local field for a contact short compared with $T_{1ρ}$, unmeasured at $1$~K. Protocols are given for $^{14}$N in NH$_3$ and deuterons in NH$_2$D.

papers.title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm
papers.abstract: Finite-element surrogates predict the stresses of a new design in one evaluation, but are usually trained on solutions with a displacement loss and compared by it, although engineering decisions rest on stresses. Application in engineering: stress analysis of perforated plates and solids with cavities, parametric families in which holes concentrate stress. Contribution to artificial intelligence: training and evaluating such surrogates in the energy norm, with or without solutions, and screening their predictions without solutions. For linear elastostatics, minimising the assembled discrete potential energy is exactly supervised regression in this norm: the energy gap of a prediction is the strain energy of its stress error. A displacement loss under-weights the stiff modes that carry the strains. In pre-registered comparisons, changing only the norm of the supervised loss cut a three-dimensional transformer's median energy-norm error 7.5-fold and its median von Mises error 6.1-fold; in two dimensions it more than halved the von Mises error, also on held-out instances. In three dimensions, the transformer trained on the energy alone came within a factor of 1.3 of the energy-norm-supervised one in median energy-norm and von Mises error. It was more accurate than the displacement-supervised one on all five metrics in every seed. Given the stiffness matrix, a Ritz projection was more accurate than the label-free transformer, in the seed means, on every metric but peak stress. No network transferred to a substantially finer mesh. The energy ranks predictions of a load case, and its sign flags those worse than the zero field.

papers.title: Beyond the First Hit: Towards Tight Guarantees for $k$-means++
papers.abstract: Let $R_k$ be the worst-case ratio between the expected cost of the $k$ seeds chosen by $k$-means++ and the optimal $k$-means cost. In their seminal paper introducing $k$-means++, Arthur and Vassilvitskii (SODA 2007) showed that $2\ln k\le R_k\le8(\ln k+2)$, and Makarychev, Reddy and Shan (NeurIPS 2020) improved the upper bound to $5(\ln k+2)$. We prove $R_k\le\frac{1163}{233}+2.108\,H_{k-2}$ for every $k\ge3$ by a computer-assisted argument, and $R_k\le5+2.3139\,H_{k-2}$ for every $k\ge2$ by a short analytic argument; here $H_j$ is the $j$th harmonic number. Since $H_{k-2}\le1+\ln k$, this lowers the leading coefficient of $\ln k$ from $5$ to $2.108$. We also determine $R_2=5$ and $R_3=185/32$ exactly; both are suprema that are approached but not attained. On the lower side we prove $R_k\ge2(1+H_{k-1})$ for every $k$, and give a second family of lower bounds that is larger than this for $2\le k\le18$. Previous analyses bound the expected cost of a cluster just after it is first sampled by a constant times its optimal cost, and then charge that cost for the rest of the run. We instead track how a cluster's cost evolves after its first hit: a cluster left with a large residual cost is likely to be sampled again before it accumulates much of the logarithmic charge, and each repeat repairs it.

papers.title: Strategic Causal Policy Learning with Manipulable Eligibility
papers.abstract: The standard rule in unconstrained causal policy learning is simple: treat individuals with nonnegative CATEs. But this rule can fail when treatment eligibility is strategically manipulable. After a policy is announced, individuals may change the covariates used for assignment without changing their underlying treatment effects. We study how such responses affect treatment allocation and welfare. Using an access-burden representation, we characterize strategic treatment and decompose welfare loss into missed beneficial treatment and harmful treatment. For linear CATEs and quadratic manipulation costs, we derive closed-form threshold corrections. When manipulation costs are homogeneous, a single correction recovers the ideal positive-CATE allocation. With heterogeneous costs, welfare maximization, pointwise safety, and minimax group welfare regret can favor different thresholds. Simulations illustrate these tradeoffs and examine the effects of estimating treatment effects and behavioral responses.

papers.title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects
papers.abstract: AI agents can automate software engineering because a compiler or a test suite checks that the code does what the user or the agent intended. In engineering analysis, however, the steps that precede the computation have few easily verifiable checks: modeling a design or an object, deciding how it is used, where supports and loads are applied, and what material each part is made of. A human expert therefore makes these decisions, carries out the steps, and judges the result, one object at a time. We present MechFoundry, an agentic loop coupled with bespoke software that automates structural analyses of real-world objects without a human in the loop. From an object's lexical description, it generates a shape, poses a loading case relevant to how the object is used, assigns a material to each part, solves the nonlinear structural response, and improves the design against the loads it carries. A differentiable GPU solver built on an adaptive octree that need not conform to the surface enables the transition from shape generation to simulation and optimization. Across 50 everyday and engineering objects, the agent posed and solved a loading case in 6.5 minutes and for US$1.3 per object on average. Without a test suite to check against, we had language-model reviewers grade each session, as a first indication of where the agent's engineering judgment holds and where it fails.

papers.title: Quantitative Gaussian limits of periodic O(N) models at and below the critical temperature
papers.abstract: We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour $O(N)$ model on periodic boxes of side $M$ in $d\ge3$, at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large $M,N$, the unnormalized $1$-Wasserstein error for the first $p\le N$ coordinates is at most $C\sqrt p (N^{-1/2}+s_M)$, where $s_M\to0$ is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$. In $d\ge5$, when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to $C(p/N+\sqrt p M^{-d})$. For fixed $p$, the sharp order is $N^{-1}+M^{-d}$ on star-containing windows and $N^{-1}$ on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.

papers.title: Divergent Trajectories in the $3x+1$ Problem and a ${\em S}$- Units Equation
papers.abstract: In this note we assume the existence of divergent trajectories (if any) under the Collatz map and investigate the consequences of this assumption, even though the Conjecture of Collatz seems to be true. In a trajectory we show that the Diophantine exponential equation $x + y = w 2^n$ in the integers $x, y, w, n$ plays an important role. In this context the recent strong finiteness theorem of Bennett and Billerey on ${\it S}-Units has consequences on the set of prime numbers generated by a collection of local minima, called wave-minima (defined ad hoc for simplicity's sake) in a divergent trajectory. It allows to define canonically a density of a trajectory and some conjectures and open problems related to these prime numbers.

papers.title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
papers.abstract: Beta-lactamases are a major mechanism of bacterial resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics; however, their functional diversity and mutational potential in environmental microbial communities remain partially understood. This study aimed to characterize environmental beta-lactamase diversity and investigate how sequence variation influences antibiotic resistance. By integrating protein language model (PLMs) with ensemble learning, we identified more than 46,000 putative beta-lactamases across all four Ambler classes from environmental metagenomes, widely distributed across diverse habitats, with distinct habitat-associated class compositions. The candidates sharing approximately 30% sequence identity with known beta-lactamases conferred resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics when expressed in Escherichia coli. Combining inverse folding model with PLMs further identified mutations that altered resistance profiles, including substitutions that increased resistance to carbapenems. Predicted high-fitness sites exhibited greater natural sequence variability overall, with higher variability in wastewater-derived than ocean-derived enzymes. These findings reveal undercharacterized beta-lactamase diversity and substantial mutational flexibility in environmental microbiomes, providing a basis for investigating their potential contribution to the diversification of antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Learning to Calibrate Jet Energies
papers.abstract: Hadronic jets are produced copiously at the Large Hadron Collider, and are a vital element of its physics program. Accurate reconstruction of their energies is therefore crucial, including correction for pile-up, detector response and data-simulation differences. Currently, each correction is performed by fitting parametric functional forms, an approach which is effective but can be fragile and challenging to extend. We present a prototype machine-learning pipeline which performs pile-up dependency removal, absolute corrections and data-mc corrections. No functional form is imposed on the correction, additional features can be easily added, and the pipeline matches or exceeds the performance of the functional approach at nearly every stage.

papers.title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
papers.abstract: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also follows from known chordality theory; the whole-component improvement uses the geometry of adjacent permutation fibres. These results complement earlier fixed-length and minimum-length orbit classifications.

papers.title: Hands-on fabrication of 2D material field-effect transistors for the classroom using off-the-shelf ionic gel
papers.abstract: We introduce a hands-on experimental method that enables students to fabricate and operate van der Waals semiconductor-based field-effect transistors (FETs) using readily available materials and minimal infrastructure. The approach is based on ionic-gel gating using commercially available hydrogel conductors originally developed for muscle electrostimulation devices. For device fabrication we rely on commercially available thin-film interdigitated electrode arrays and for the semiconductor channel, we deposited MoS2 flakes produced by high-throughput mechanical exfoliation. By avoiding the need for cleanroom processing, vacuum deposition, or custom electrolytes, this method allows functional FETs based on van der Waals materials to be realized in a standard teaching laboratory. The experiment is well suited for undergraduate and early graduate courses and is intended to complement concepts introduced in electronics and solid-state physics by providing students with first-hand experience in the fabrication and electrical characterization of emerging electronic devices. Representative electrical measurements demonstrate gate-dependent modulation of the channel conductance and illustrate characteristic features of ionic-gated transistor operation. Overall, the proposed platform provides an accessible route for students to fabricate, characterize, and analyze field-effect devices without access to conventional semiconductor foundry.

papers.title: The Market Is the Reward: Design Markets, Not Just Traders for Human-AI Collective Intelligence
papers.abstract: Learning agents are becoming market participants, yet machine learning still treats the market as a fixed environment, although its payoff rule is the reward agents learn from. This position paper argues that financial AI should build HyperMarkets for human-AI collective intelligence, and not only the agents that trade in them: markets whose liquidity provision, information production, outcome determination, and trading rule are performed or adapted by learning agents and designed jointly toward explicit market-level objectives. In a pre-registered simulation with Claude agents trading for principals, joint design raises a market-level objective by 79% over separately tuned functions, through a trading rule that helps only when slow traders are present, and how evidence is paid for decides whether a stronger agent earns more for its principal. We state when fixed rules or non-market aggregation should be preferred and what findings would refute the case.

papers.title: SuSy and CoDy Radiation from Evaporating Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between physics beyond the Standard Model and modified spacetime geometries in shaping the photon and neutrino spectra from evaporating black holes. We implement three representative supersymmetric (SuSy) benchmarks and a composite dynamics (CoDy) scenario in BlackHawk. We consider both Schwarzschild black holes and regular black holes geometries, namely polymerized, Hayward, and Simpson--Visser black holes. New degrees of freedom at the TeV scale become accessible at Hawking temperatures corresponding to black hole masses of approximately $M_{\rm BH}\sim 10^{10}\,\mathrm{g}$. We show that physics beyond the Standard Model produces distinctive signatures in both the instantaneous secondary-photon and neutrino spectra. Radiative decays generate narrow spectral features with approximately temperature-independent relative amplitudes, while multistep decay cascades produce broad enhancements that become increasingly pronounced at higher temperatures. In contrast, compressed mass spectra exhibit no localized features. Crucially, we show that the effects of new particle physics and modified spacetime geometries can become intertwined in specific energy regimes, altering the resulting spectral signatures. Our results demonstrate that photon and neutrino spectra provide complementary probes of new particle physics and black hole geometry, with predicted spectral enhancements extending into the energy ranges accessible to current and future high-energy observatories.

papers.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
papers.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is almost an order of magnitude faster than a comparable FEM. Finally, the Neural Physics method is applied to a real-world test case with integrated experimental data and simulates the infiltration of water through a rain garden. This new approach therefore provides a route to efficiently and accurately solve Richards equation for a wide array of hydrological applications.

papers.title: Provenance-tracked, experimentally validated neural operator surrogates of three-dimensional laser melting with keyholes and free-form paths
papers.abstract: A three-dimensional thermo-fluid-dynamic simulation of laser melting resolves the melt pool and vapor depression but costs from one to thousands of core-hours per track. We train FNO, RIGNO and GAOT neural operators that predict the temperature, melt-pool and free-surface fields. Our datasets comprise 3D temperature and melt geometry fields covering lack-of-fusion to keyhole conditions under varied laser power, scan speed, beam radius, beam shape and preheat, and include free-form scan paths with speed changes and up to four beams. We generate them with FLOW-3D WELD, using solver settings validated against published measurements for four materials. We implement an AiiDA framework to store the provenance of every simulation, model and evaluation, so each tabulated metric traces back to the solver and model inputs behind it. On held-out simulations, the best architecture scores below 2 % relative temperature error on quasi-steady straight tracks, below 4 % on single-beam free-form paths and about 5 % with two to four beams. Inference takes under a second per predicted arbitrary time step on our single-GPU setup. We extend a surrogate trained on Ti-6Al-4V to Inconel 718 by growing its training set autonomously, and the extended models reach a relative temperature error of about 3 % or less on both Inconel 718 and Ti-6Al-4V. At 20 Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 718 conditions held out of training, the two-alloy RIGNO predicts melt-pool and vapor-depression depths within 30 % of published measurements, and its depths differ from FLOW-3D at the same conditions by 2 % on average. Furthermore, these results provide a scalable framework which can readily be applied to computationally intensive simulations in fields other than laser melting.

papers.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
papers.abstract: Identifying a tumor's DNA mutations is central to cancer diagnosis and treatment, but distinguishing genuine mutations from sequencing artifacts is error-prone. In practice, genuine mutations are identified using fixed variant-allele-frequency (VAF) and depth thresholds which cannot separate artifacts from genuine mutations in the borderline low-VAF zone where they overlap. A laboratory specialist must manually inspect the read-level sequencing data, a slow step that has high inter-rater variability and causes diagnosis delays. We present AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication; an agentic framework that automates this read-level inspection with subagents that reason over evidence, generate investigative code, and return a real-or-artifact adjudications with an auditable reasoning trace all without training on existing data. On both the SEQC2 DNA-seq benchmark and patient RNA-seq data, restricted to a subsample of borderline variants where thresholds fail, both closed-source (Claude Sonnet 5) and open-weight (GLM 5.3 Flash and Gemma 4 31b) agents outperform the best achievable VAF/depth thresholds. Ultimately, AVA is suited for privacy-constrained clinical deployment, since the framework can run on locally deployed open-weight models with descriptive reasoning traces to keep specialists in the loop.

papers.title: Predicting transcriptional interactions with GrnPFN
papers.abstract: Combinatorial therapies offer opportunities to improve treatment efficacy and overcome therapeutic resistance, but their rational design requires understanding how combined interventions interact beyond their individual effects. Combined genetic and chemical perturbations can elicit nonadditive transcriptional responses, yet the vast number of possible combinations limits experimental characterization. Predicting these interactions is particularly challenging when few or no combinations have been measured. Here we present GrnPFN, a prior-data fitted network that predicts nonadditive transcriptional responses to combinations from single-perturbation profiles. Pretrained on simulated screens generated from random gene-regulatory networks, GrnPFN incorporates measured combinations through in-context learning without retraining. We evaluated GrnPFN in single-cell screens spanning CRISPR activation, RNA knockdown and drug combinations, using separate cells to construct model inputs, training targets and test targets. Without measured combinations in the target screen, GrnPFN outperformed gradient boosting trained on other screens. With limited combination measurements, it outperformed kernel ridge regression fitted to the same measured pairs. These advantages extended to an additional screen combining CRISPR interference with a drug. Our results demonstrate that pretraining on simulated regulatory networks enables prediction of nonadditive transcriptional interactions across perturbation modalities when experimental measurements are scarce.

papers.title: Selecting Person Segmentation Models for Real-Time Video Call Backgrounds on the CPU
papers.abstract: Background blur and background replacement are now normal parts of a video call. Many open models and open source pipelines can do this, but it is hard to know which one to pick. Speed, edge quality and license all matter, and they are often reported on different hardware, or not reported at all. In this work we ran 20 setups on the same laptop CPU, with the same 640x480 frames and the same output view. The setups are 15 open models and 5 complete open source pipelines. We measured frames per second on a test clip and on a live webcam, compared the masks on a public domain portrait and on three video call photos with a raised hand, one of them a close front camera view, and recorded the license of every model. The fastest setups reach more than 40 frames per second on a laptop CPU, while the slowest, a high detail model for still images, needs several seconds per frame. A few setups give clean edges and still run in real time. We also found that the runtime library and the steps around the model can change the speed by several times. Based on these results we give a guide that tells the reader which model to choose for a given need, such as a weak laptop, the best hair edges, a closed source product, or people behind the speaker.

papers.title: Probe Before You Preach: Conformal Ambiguity Sets and Neuro-Symbolic Counterfactual Probing for Diagnosing Algebraic Misconceptions in Middle School Mathematics
papers.abstract: Distinct mathematical misconception rules can produce the same incorrect answer, making diagnosis from a single response ambiguous. We formalize this algebraic collision and derive a conditional Bayes error bound; internally generated reasoning does not add student-specific information beyond its inputs under an explicit conditional-independence assumption. We propose Mondrian Adaptive Conformal Misconception Sets (MACMS) and Symbolic-Verified Counterfactual Micro-Probing (Sym-EIG). MACMS has curriculum-group marginal coverage under exchangeability, not a per-student correctness guarantee. Sym-EIG searches for probes whose outputs separate modeled candidate rules; identification additionally depends on the candidate set and response model. An audit of a local public Eedi graph finds 2,118 of 2,258 linked constructs associated with at least two misconception IDs; construct-level associations alone do not establish same-answer collisions. Other project performance tables require recomputation because their script assigns numerical results directly. No diagnostic performance or classroom learning benefit is claimed here. A classroom study is proposed for future validation.

papers.title: Energy exchange confined to the perturbations: the frozen dark sector confronted with Planck, DESI, supernovae and cosmic shear
papers.abstract: We present cosmological constraints on the frozen model, in which dark matter and dark energy exchange energy only at the level of the perturbations. The expansion history is that of flat $Λ$CDM, while on sub-horizon scales a dimensionless coupling $Σ$ enhances ($Σ<0$) or suppresses ($Σ>0$) the growth of the dark-matter density contrast. We use Planck 2018 CMB and lensing data, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the DES five-year supernovae (Dovekie recalibration), and the KiDS-Legacy and DES Year 3 cosmic-shear amplitudes, corrected for the model's growth. Planck alone gives $Σ=-0.22\pm0.11$, a preference driven by the lensing smoothing of the acoustic peaks and the low large-scale temperature power. Since BAO and supernovae do not constrain $Σ$, the coupling acts only through the Planck posterior, lowering the Planck--DESI tension from $1.9σ$ to $1.0$--$1.5σ$, and that between Planck plus supernovae and DESI from $2.4$--$2.5σ$ to $1.7$--$2.1σ$. Combining Planck, DESI and supernovae we find $Σ=-0.24\pm0.09$ and $\ln B=1.5$ relative to $Λ$CDM, a preference that vanishes when the strongest-coupling region is excluded. The enhanced growth, however, raises the Planck--shear tension from $1.9σ$ to $2.5$--$2.7σ$. With shear included, $Σ=0.01\pm0.08$ and $S_8=0.808\pm0.025$, while $\ln B=-1.3$ favors $Λ$CDM. $H_0$ and the age of the Universe agree with $Λ$CDM for every data combination, and the SH0ES discrepancy remains at $4.4σ$. Without shear, the favored coupling predicts half the $Λ$CDM integrated Sachs--Wolfe amplitude at $z=0.5$ and an enhanced shear signal in the lowest tomographic bins. These signatures and the redshift distribution of cluster counts test the coupling independently of the amplitude of the fluctuations.

papers.title: Frames and representing systems in Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: We study representing systems of Cauchy kernels or dilations of a given function in Hardy spaces. We give a complete geometric description of countable sets $Λ\subset \mathbb{D}$ such that the system $\{\hat{k}_λ\}_{λ\in Λ}$ of normalized Cauchy kernels forms a generalized frame in the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{D})$ with $p \in (1, \infty)$ with respect to a particular coefficient space. For a wide class of functions we construct representing systems of their dilations in $H^2$. We also obtain a linear method for expanding functions in series of Cauchy kernels in $H^2$.

papers.title: Optical and ADM Tomography from Directed Causal Arrival Times
papers.abstract: We formulate a local reconstruction of Lorentzian geometry from directed null arrival times and spacetime volume, assuming a supplied clock foliation and spatial coordinate gauge. Static arrival data recover the optical metric $\bar h=N^{-2}h$, while a normalized volume density fixes the remaining conformal scale up to a global constant. In the stationary case, the Randers arrival function separates optical geometry and shift. For time-dependent ADM metrics we derive the exact future null indicatrix, its algebraic inverse, and a minimal finite-direction sampling scheme: $d(d+3)/2$ one-way arrival measurements suffice in $d$ spatial dimensions, are necessary for stable local recovery within the specified scalar-measurement class, and admit an exact semialgebraic consistency test with certified robustness and rejection margins under bounded measurement error. A short-time freezing estimate and finite-resolution inverse give metric error $O(a/ε+ε+ζ)$ for arrival error $a$, probe scale $ε$, and volume error $ζ$; optimizing yields $O(\sqrt a+ζ)$. Algebraic and numerical checks reproduce the inversion and stability formulas. The result is an operational, gauge-conditional tomography theorem; it does not infer the clocks or arrival oracle from a background-free quantum theory.

papers.title: Joint Bayesian Inference of Dense Matter and f(Q) Gravity with Nuclear and Neutron Star Constraints
papers.abstract: We investigate neutron star (NS) properties in symmetric teleparallel $f(Q)$ gravity while consistently accounting for uncertainties in the dense matter equation of state (EOS). We focus on the linear $f(Q)$ model and perform a joint Bayesian inference of the nuclear matter and modified gravity parameters using a Taylor expansion EOS around nuclear saturation density. The analysis incorporates complementary constraints from nuclear saturation properties, chiral effective field theory calculations of pure neutron matter, heavy-ion collision, and empirical nuclear data, the GW170817 tidal deformability posterior, and NICER mass--radius measurements. The resulting posterior distributions simultaneously constrain the dense matter and gravity sectors and quantify their correlations within a common framework. For a canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NS, we obtain $R_{1.4}=11.28^{+0.35}_{-0.31}\,\mathrm{km}$ and $Λ_{1.4}=151.4^{+44.9}_{-31.2}$, while the maximum mass is constrained to $M_{\rm max}=2.22^{+0.29}_{-0.16}\,M_\odot$. The modified gravity parameters exhibit only weak direct correlations with most stellar observables, while a pronounced degeneracy remains within the gravity sector. Our results show that accounting for EOS uncertainties is essential for quantifying the interplay between dense matter physics and modified gravity and provide a systematic framework for confronting symmetric teleparallel gravity with nuclear and multimessenger NS observations.

papers.title: Piecewise Interpretations in Many-Sorted Logic
papers.abstract: Piecewise interpretations, introduced by Visser, generalize ordinary interpretations between first-order theories by allowing formulae to be interpreted using disjoint unions of definable sets. This makes it possible to capture natural constructions, such as the projective completion of an affine plane, but also leads to a notion of equivalence of theories, namely piecewise bi-interpretability. We develop the theory of piecewise interpretations systematically in the many-sorted setting. Each piecewise interpretation induces a semantic dual, a functor between categories of models. In addition, we introduce a syntactic notion of morphism between piecewise interpretations, which likewise has a semantic dual. Using these semantic duals, we collect theories, piecewise interpretations, and morphisms between them into a bicategory, in particular defining a well-behaved notion of composition of interpretations, associative up to coherent isomorphism. As an application, we consider a familiar idea, championed by Quine, namely that one can replace any many-sorted theory with a corresponding single-sorted one by replacing sorts with sortal predicates. We show that this leads to a biequivalence between the developed bicategories of theories with finitely many sorts and single-sorted theories, thereby providing an argument for the dispensability of sorts.

papers.title: Finite bases for matrix semirings: transfer theorems and nilpotent counterexamples
papers.abstract: We first show that the nonfinitely based six-element ai-semiring $SR_6$ has finitely based full matrix semirings for every $n\ge2$, with a four-identity basis relative to the ai-semiring axioms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first known example of this phenomenon. We then construct a countably infinite flat ai-semiring $P$ whose scalar and two-by-two matrix varieties are nonfinitely based, whereas its matrix varieties in sizes $n\ge3$ admit a five-identity relative basis. For both examples, the intervals from the scalar variety to each matrix variety of size at least two have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Finally, we establish transfer results for stronger forms of nonfinite basability and a finite-basis dichotomy for matrix semirings of size at least two over scalars with a genuine zero generating a locally finite variety: finite basability in the multiplicatively nilpotent case, and inherent nonfinite basability otherwise.

papers.title: Quivers with potential for quantum affine superalgebras
papers.abstract: We construct a surjective algebra homomorphism from the $K$-theoretic Hall algebras of certain quivers with potential to the (half) quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras.

papers.title: Another Multivector Inverse Algorithm
papers.abstract: A numerical algorithm is described for computing the inverse of a non-singular multivector across dimensions. The method wraps a reversion-like product around a Faddeev--LeVerrier--Souriau (FLS) polynomial core. While FLS provides dimensional extensibility, the wrapper reduces the polynomial order of the FLS method, and introduces a sparse multivector which can be further exploited. The construction and essential properties of the initial involution are explained. For dimensions 4--7, the optimized inverse requires fewer real multiplications than a same-dimension multivector product. Dimensions 8--11 follow easily on common hardware with similar efficiency. For dimensions 12--15, higher-precision arithmetic demonstrates the generality of the algorithm when the arithmetic can support it. Performance on common hardware is reported. Directions are included for obtaining a Python package with examples for numerical computation in Clifford algebra, supporting arbitrary signatures including degenerate cases.

papers.title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Can a coding agent fix a user's repository while also completing and delivering work the user never requested? In this paper, we introduce SideTaskBench to measure this failure where third-party technical references induce agents to produce independent side-task artifacts during an authorized repair. Repair success alone misses this behavior. Our key measurement contribution is to pair each repair with a self-contained side task and verify side tasks' delivery success rate along with the repair success rate. The benchmark contains 25 Python repairs and 190 side-task units. Its four-level similarity index defines 300 executable repair--side-task pairs. The experiments show roughly 40% valid delivery under wrapped requests for two models, alongside repair success close to their clean baselines. The completed v10 similarity run uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash on all 300 pairs, with eight repetitions per pair (2,400 runs). Conditional delivery ranges from 20.48% for L0 unrelated tasks to 57.44% for L3 mechanism-overlapping tasks, while the L1-L0 difference is 5.37 percentage points and remains sensitive to task composition. The central insight is that technical relevance may blur the authorization boundary for an agent, such that an agent can solve the requested problem and still deliver unauthorized work. SideTaskBench emphasizes this potential weakness of existing agents and provides a testbed for defenses that preserve repair capability while preventing unauthorized delivery. The code is available at: https://github.com/xywen97/SideTaskBench.

papers.title: Involutive Duality of Lie Operators in the Extended Alpha Group
papers.abstract: This work investigates the involutive, adjoint, and spectral structures arising in the extended Alpha Group. Starting from the four-dimensional Alpha Group transformation matrix, whose angular depen- dence is governed by coupled tan θ and cot θ modes, an iterative commutator procedure generates a sixteen-dimensional real Lie algebra. Within this algebra, the operators B5 and B6 are identified as structurally distinguished elements and analyzed through their adjoint actions. The operator B6 is veri- fied to be involutive and induces an 8 + 8 decomposition of the Lie algebra, while the adjoint action of B5 defines an eight-dimensional invariant mixed sector through a polynomial kernel. The restricted adjoint operators preserve this sector, and their coupled action generates an idempotent operator Q, satisfying Q2 = Q, revealing an invariant projective structure. The spectral analysis further identifies characteristic- polynomial factorizations associated with B5 , B6 , and their compositions, including golden-ratio relations among distinct generators of the extended algebra. These results establish structural connections between the original modal representation, Lie-algebraic involution, adjoint dynamics, projective organization, and the spectral structure of the extended Alpha Group.

papers.title: The Sprague--Grundy Function of Slow Exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ Piles
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for the normal-play Sprague--Grundy (SG) function of slow exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ piles. A move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. A truncation preserves every legal move sequence. The SG value depends only on the total of the truncated coordinates modulo $2k$, their number of odd entries, and the parities of the two smallest piles. For every $k\geq2$, the set of the SG values is $\{0,1,2,3\}$. We prove the formula by the mex characterization, including the reductions needed after boundary moves. We also prove a unit-shift identity and use it with a known optimal-move theorem to explain the four-value bound independently of the explicit formula.

papers.title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
papers.abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, and each token reads every weight from memory, so on edge devices, decoding is limited by memory bandwidth. 2:4 semi-structured sparsity keeps two of every four weights, but Apple-silicon GPUs have no sparse matrix hardware, so pruning helps only if a kernel actually reads fewer bytes. We present metalSPARSE, to our knowledge the first 2:4 sparse kernels for Apple GPUs, together with a fused decoder written in Metal. The kernels stream weights in compressed form and expand them in registers. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity on every decoder linear layer, decoding runs 3.6x faster than HuggingFace Transformers on PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x faster than MLX on a 16 GB M4. The same engine on dense weights matches MLX, so the gain comes from the compressed weights, and sparsity delivers 97% of the speedup its byte reduction allows. Prompt processing, which is compute-bound, does not speed up. To preserve quality, we combine a Wanda mask with block-wise reconstruction and low-rank adapters trained jointly with the surviving weights and quantized to 4 bits. On WikiText-2 this brings perplexity from 3.01x dense after one-shot pruning (Wanda with a closed-form refit) to 1.34x, and the whole pipeline runs on the same laptop/hardware.

papers.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
papers.abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.

papers.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
papers.abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gröbner basis elimination.

papers.title: Modelling the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related home insurance claims
papers.abstract: We study the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related claims in private home insurance, combining detailed portfolio and claim information with publicly available high-resolution weather data. Existing approaches typically start from an identified severe weather event, such as a hailstorm, and model the dynamics of the claims caused by that event. In practice, however, claims arise under moderate as well as severe conditions, and the claims handling process runs continuously. An insurer therefore requires insight into the occurrence and reporting of claims on every calendar day. Modelling all calendar days jointly poses two challenges: recently occurred claims are only partially reported, and days with severe weather are rare while accounting for a large share of the claims. We propose a multi-regime EM-XGBoost framework that addresses both: an expectation-maximisation setup accounts for the incurred-but-not-reported (IBNR) claims, while a data-driven regime structure lets the occurrence and reporting dynamics differ across weather conditions. In a case study on a Dutch home insurance portfolio, we compare single- and two-regime specifications for two spatial resolutions: the country as a whole, and its individual regions. We find that the regional two-regime model outperforms the regional single-regime model as well as both national models, indicating that the benefit of a multi-regime setting depends on a sufficiently granular spatial resolution. We also show that daily covariates constructed from hourly weather observations, capturing the duration and the intra-day timing of severe weather, improve both the occurrence and the reporting model.

papers.title: Bayesian Evidence Fusion for Capability Tracking-A Simulation Study and Historical CI Pilot
papers.abstract: SaaS capability assessments can become stale between questionnaires, while delivery telemetry offers incomplete and correlated evidence. Continuous assessment and Bayesian delivery analysis already exist, leaving uncertainty about how biased surveys and missing observations should influence capability estimates.We implement SAAS-MATURITY-TWIN, an anchored Gaussian state model that jointly filters capability proxies and persistent survey offsets. Source covariance prevents correlated observations from being counted independently. Conditional uncertainty supports forecasting and budgeted intervention screening, with action effects estimated from randomized synthetic cohorts. Ten seeds generate forty paired worlds spanning reference observations, extensive missingness, informative missingness, and increased noise. Reference latent root mean squared error is 0.1261, compared with 0.1452 for a tuned moving average; nominal ninety percent intervals cover 90.3 percent. Improved state recovery produces only small incident forecasting differences. Adaptive conformal inference and an adapted conformal PID controller are evaluated separately for observed telemetry, where noise shifts expose calibration limitations. A licensed TravisTorrent pilot evaluates build prediction on 13 074 held out builds from 224 projects. Logistic regression achieves a Brier score of 0.1289, close to random forests. These results support reproducible methodological testing, but do not establish real organizational maturity, intervention effectiveness, or production readiness. Independent calibration and longitudinal validation remain necessary.

papers.title: Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: The integration of mechanistic signaling networks into clinical research has become a cornerstone of precision oncology. By capturing the complex biochemical interactions within a cell, these networks provide a functional map of disease progression that goes beyond simple genomic mutations. Consequently, the development of specific signaling models of patients has significant relevance, allowing for a more granular representation of individual disease profiles. In this setting, there is a growing need for robust methodologies capable of comparing graph based pathway structures to identify similarities and differences across patient cohorts. Such comparisons are essential for the identification of clinically meaningful subgroups, and the discovery of novel biomarkers. Standard graph kernels, while mathematically rigorous, often remain too generic for this purpose. They frequently fail to capture features specific to gene signaling networks, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance. In this paper, we present a domain specific graph kernel designed for mechanistic signaling networks. Unlike generic approaches, our method explicitly incorporates biological constraints and gene interaction patterns into the kernel formulation, enabling a more accurate characterization of both topological structure and functional behavior. We assess its performance on breast cancer datasets, focusing on its ability to support disease subtyping. Our results suggest that our approach can effectively contribute to patient stratification.

papers.title: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery
papers.abstract: Corrections for backtest overfitting such as the deflated Sharpe ratio are applied after a search ends: the searcher maximises raw performance and a separate procedure deflates the reported winner. Autonomous searches driven by large language models perform many implicit backtests before reporting, so this paper asks what changes when the correction moves inside the loop and the acceptance threshold is indexed to the running count and dispersion of the search's own trials. The threshold then becomes an object the search can optimise against: we show analytically that a naive in-loop bar admits a variance-dilution effect, in which mediocre near-duplicate candidates lower the bar because the ledger's dispersion falls faster than its trial-count factor grows. We propose two defences, a pre-registered variance floor and a monotone high-water-mark bar, and evaluate the construction under a protocol frozen before any run, with every in-loop decision replaying exactly from its recorded trace. Across 53 audited hundred-candidate searches over two frontier models, two universes, and two feature spaces, the gated search reports "no certifiable discovery" on 36 of 37 runs, un-gated controls report a strategy on all 16, and every arm's out-of-sample confidence interval includes zero. Supporting studies find that state-based stopping reaches the same outcome after 8 to 9 trials at about a twelfth of the trial budget while an adaptive budget adds nothing, that a controlled stress test reproduces the dilution effect and both defences, and that a hundred nominal trials collapse to 6 to 8 effectively independent return streams. We scope these results to the analysed system.

papers.title: A Hidden Markov Analysis of Wet-Weather Tyre Crossover in Formula One
papers.abstract: Detecting a wet-weather regime and deciding when to replace slick tyres are distinct tasks. This study examines their relationship through a retrospective analysis of the 2024 British Grand Prix. A three-state hidden Markov model (HMM) represents normalized lap time and precipitation, while an entry rule requires both a high filtered Wet-state probability and sufficient pace deterioration. The analysis includes 642 car-laps and 33 complete lap-bin observations within the available precipitation record. Each completed-lap signal takes effect on the following lap. The combined rule enters on lap 27, matching the team-weighted modal reference; removing the pace or state condition advances entry to laps 25 and 20, respectively. The combined entry is retained in all 10 team-exclusion refits, but refitting a specification with larger off-diagonal transition probabilities produces entry on lap 20. These comparisons illustrate how state inference can contextualize a performance criterion while exposing dependence on model assumptions. Because estimation and rule development use the same event, the correspondence establishes neither prospective accuracy nor a race-time advantage.

papers.title: Modeling Drug Overdose Mortality Levels Using Social Vulnerability Indicators in U.S. Counties: A Double Machine Learning Approach for Causal Analysis
papers.abstract: Drug poisoning mortality (DPM) remains a leading cause of death among working-age Americans, and its burden falls unevenly across communities. Existing county-level studies of social vulnerability and overdose have largely reported predictive or associational relationships, while the shape of the adjusted exposure-response relationship between overall social vulnerability and mortality remains unclear. We examined the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and county drug poisoning mortality across three two-year windows spanning 2016-2021. The associational analysis compared linear regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost models of log mortality using period-specific SVI subfeatures and county covariates. The selected XGBoost models were interpreted with SHAP values. The double machine learning (DML) analysis estimated the exposure-response relationship between SVI and DPM and tested the linearity restriction. Socioeconomic vulnerability contributed positively to predicted mortality, with disability and unemployment among the strongest subfeatures, while racial and ethnic minority composition contributed negatively in all three periods. Summing the four theme contributions reduced the overall-index attribution by 34% to 36%, indicating substantial offsetting. Linearity was rejected in every window ($p < 10^{-26}$). The adjusted relationship increased through the middle of the SVI distribution and declined in the upper tail. This pattern remained stable both before and after the outbreak of the epidemic. Overall SVI therefore captured meaningful variation in overdose mortality but did not function as a uniformly increasing risk scale across its full range. Component-level interpretation and current overdose surveillance provide important context for interpreting the composite index.

papers.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones
papers.abstract: Real-time urban traffic monitoring is essential for modern city management, yet conventional static sensors provide only limited spatial coverage. Autonomous drone fleets can complement this infrastructure by offering flexible, high-resolution mobile sensing across different parts of the network. This paper introduces a spatio-temporal Gaussian process (GP) framework for reconstructing network-wide traffic states from partial aerial observations. The model accounts for the physical structure of the road network through a graph Matérn kernel, which embeds network topology into the spatial covariance structure, and captures temporal dependencies through an exponential temporal kernel. Within this framework, historical loop detector data provide an informative prior mean that is updated in real time using incoming drone observations, yielding network-wide point estimates together with predictive uncertainty. We validate our framework in two distinct case studies: a microscopic simulation of Barcelona and real-world drone data from Athens. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms historical baselines in estimating and predicting Vehicle Hours Traveled (VHT), notably reducing the required fleet size. Furthermore, leveraging the model's predictive uncertainty to guide drone movements yields additional performance gains, highlighting the potential for future uncertainty-aware fleet routing algorithms.

papers.title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
papers.abstract: This study benchmarks 24 forecasting configurations on ESHED-38, daily smart-meter consumption for 38 homes in Erbil, Iraq, collected from May 2020 to June 2025 with station weather and a household survey. The configurations span five base families, plus two cross-family ensembles: naive baselines, per-house statistical models, global gradient-boosted trees, global deep networks, and zero-shot time-series foundation models. All are evaluated on the same 54,720 forecasts from 48 weekly origins over a 359-day held-out period, at lead times up to 30 days, using scaled absolute error, the continuous ranked probability score, calibration, and Friedman, Nemenyi and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests. The best configurations cut the scaled error of a seasonal-naive forecast by 20 to 25 percent, and the leading models beat it in all 38 houses. Chronos-2, used without training, is significantly the most accurate model one day ahead; at one week it is statistically tied with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and a pre-specified ensemble, and the two ensembles lead at 30 days. Deep networks trained from scratch do not outperform exponential smoothing on average, and the household survey adds negligible skill. Metered demand peaks in winter and falls as temperature rises. Recorded weather did not improve any model run with and without it. A quality screen helps explain why: on 68 percent of dates a temperature value recurs exactly on other dates, in three annual blocks covering almost all of the test period, suggesting that much of the weather record reuses one annual sequence. The value of weather information is therefore treated as unresolved, and the protocol is released as a baseline.

papers.title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method
papers.abstract: Fluid flow networks, from pipeline infrastructure to biological vasculature, are governed by nonlinear edgewise hyperbolic laws coupled through continuity and conservation at junctions. Many-query tasks require rapid evaluation across unseen parametric settings, but conventional methods re-solve the system for each query at prohibitive cost. Existing physics-informed neural approaches impose the governing equations through penalty losses over generic neural approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, with no guarantee that their reduction reduces solution error, and the resulting optimization is prone to ill-conditioning, particularly for hyperbolic systems. Building on the "representation-then-projection" principle of the neural basis method, we introduce a new approach for modeling fluid flow networks. Fixed neural bases define the representation space on each edge, while projection of the discretized equations determines the expansion coefficients, embedding edgewise laws into a conservative formulation. Edge subdomains are coupled through non-overlapping domain decomposition, and a neural operator learns, directly in this reduced space, the parametric map to the expansion coefficients. On looped and branching network topologies, we reproduce references with relative $L^2$ errors below 0.02%, whereas the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. Across unseen boundary conditions in both interpolation and extrapolation, we maintain mean pressure errors below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%, while the physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors. These results highlight the framework's potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

papers.title: Quantifying Methodological Inflation in Clinical Machine Learning: A Cross-Modality Audit of Subject-Level Leakage and Nested Feature Selection for Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Reported accuracy in Parkinson's disease (PD) machine learning can reflect the evaluation protocol rather than real signal. We ask how much evaluation choices inflate performance by comparing naive and rigorous protocols on voice, telemonitoring and blood-transcriptomic datasets. Subject-aware splitting reduced voice AUROC from 0.892 to 0.780 and telemonitoring R^2 from 0.105 to -0.037; Random Forest recovered neither gap. Supervised probe selection before splitting inflated transcriptomic AUROC from 0.711 to 0.998. A nested 50-probe panel matched a 1,000-probe panel (0.811 versus 0.844), and recruitment-wave batch structure was detected. Future work should validate a stable panel on an independent cohort.

papers.title: Enhancing Resolution and Reliability with Attention Mechanisms in Nuclear Accident Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: Severe accident (SA) analysis of nuclear power plants relies on system codes such as MAAP, whose computational cost limits large-scale applications including dynamic probabilistic safety assessment and reinforcement learning. This study proposes the Accident Binary-Continuous Transformer (ABC-Transformer), a decoder-only surrogate combining causal self-attention with temporal attention pooling. It jointly embeds continuous thermal-hydraulic variables with binary safety-system and severe accident management guideline (SAMG) states, enabling 5-minute-resolution forecasting over 72-hour transients. Trained on 11,000 MAAP simulations of a total loss of component cooling water scenario for the OPR1000, it achieved lower one-step teacher-forcing error than CNN and recurrent baselines at fine resolutions. Autoregressive reliability was characterized as a full per-scenario distribution over 1100 held-out scenarios. For scheduled-sampling (SS) training, the median $R^2$ is $0.947 \pm 0.006$ and $3.8 \pm 1.0$% of scenarios fail ($R^2<0$; mean $\pm$ SD over four training seeds), while errors accumulate with rollout length. A Mahalanobis self-distance computed from each surrogate rollout, before comparison with the MAAP reference, ranks these failures (ROC-AUC 0.895, reference seed). A threshold at the 40th percentile of calibration scores accepts $36.8 \pm 0.5$% of 550 evaluation scenarios, with no accepted rollout below $R^2 = 0$ for any seed, and routes the rest to MAAP.

papers.title: Time-Domain and Spectral Decomposition of Dynamic Coupling with Instantaneous and Time-Lagged Causality: Methodological Evaluation and Application to Cardiovascular Variability
papers.abstract: The quantification of dynamic interactions in coupled physiological time series is a central question in biomedical signal processing. A critical issue is the presence of instantaneous dependencies, often neglected in conventional Granger causality (GC) analyses despite potentially reflecting physiologically meaningful effects. We investigate time- and frequency-domain measures of causality within the linear autoregressive (AR) framework, treating instantaneous dependencies according to three formulations: (i) the classical strictly causal AR model, providing spectral measures of time-lagged GC and instantaneous interaction; (ii) the Geweke approach, assigning instantaneous dependencies to the direction opposite to that under investigation; (iii) a single extended AR model incorporating causally-oriented instantaneous dependencies, yielding spectral GC measures accounting for both instantaneous and time-lagged causality. The three approaches are evaluated in simulated Gaussian systems, where dynamic measures can be derived analytically and compared with the expected coupling structure. The single extended AR model emerges as the most consistent formulation when instantaneous dependencies have a physiologically meaningful causal direction and is then applied to cardiovascular interactions between heart period (HP) and systolic (SAP) or diastolic arterial pressure (DAP) in healthy subjects during postural and mental stress. Accounting for instantaneous dependencies substantially affects HP-SAP and HP-DAP interactions, enabling better quantification of baroreflex and cardiac run-off mechanisms and characterization of their responses to stress and of low- and high-frequency dynamics. Overall, the framework provides consistent representation of causal interactions across time and frequency and highlights the importance of accounting for instantaneous dependencies in physiological coupling.

papers.title: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Forecasting of Sparse Counts with Exposure: An Application to Airline Demand and Premium-Cabin Capacity Sharing
papers.abstract: Sparse count forecasting arises when events are rare, exposure varies across observational units, and short histories contain many zeros. Using thin-market airline demand as a motivating application, this paper develops a hierarchical exposure-adjusted Poisson-Gamma (HEPG) framework for probabilistic forecasting. Conditional counts follow a Poisson model with an exposure offset and pooled calendar effects, while unit specific baseline intensities receive a Gamma prior whose hyperparameters are estimated empirically across the population. The resulting posterior is Gamma and the posterior predictive distribution is negative binomial, providing closed-form partial pooling and explicit propagation of parameter uncertainty. This is especially useful for zero-history or low-exposure units, where independent maximum-likelihood estimates are unstable or collapse to zero. An adaptive extension, A-HEPG, adds a moment-matched negative-binomial variance correction when residual extra-Poisson variation remains. In synthetic experiments with 400 heterogeneous markets, HEPG improves average negative log predictive probability relative to complete pooling and independent route-level Poisson estimation. At a mean latent rate of 0.15 requests per exposure unit, the score is 0.525 for HEPG, compared with 0.585 for pooled Poisson and 0.731 for route-level Poisson maximum likelihood. Under strong overdispersion, A-HEPG reduces the score from 0.552 to 0.529. A downstream cabin-capacity example links the predictive distribution to a seat-protection rule based on predictive survival probabilities and fare ratios. The study emphasizes coherent probabilistic inference, partial pooling, and diagnostic model escalation for sparse applied count data.

papers.title: Clustering trajectories of modelled estimates: an uncertainty-aware framework, with an application to global cardiovascular disease burden, 1990 to 2023
papers.abstract: Modelled health estimates such as those of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study are increasingly used in secondary analyses designed for observed data. However, trajectory clustering typically ignores published uncertainty, selects the number of clusters using criteria blind to it, and assigns countries to groups with unwarranted certainty. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that separates trajectory level from shape, quantifies membership probabilities by perturbing estimates within their uncertainty intervals, selects clusters based on stability under uncertainty, and examines the roles of development, region, and measurement quality. Applied to age-standardised cardiovascular disease DALY rates for 201 countries from 1990-2023 (GBD 2023), the framework identified two stable trajectory types, whereas the gap statistic selected three. The additional cluster was poorly supported (median membership probability 0.70) and disappeared once uncertainty was considered. The retained clusters had similar burdens in 1990 but diverged markedly over time: a stalled-improvement group of 78 countries (median change $-8\%$, 40 of them in sub-Saharan Africa) and a sustained-decline group of 92 countries ($-52\%$). Thirty-one countries remained unclassified because their memberships were uncertain. Results were reproduced using mortality rates, a 2000-2023 analysis window, and bootstrap resampling. Among countries with the narrowest uncertainty intervals, a third well-supported trajectory emerged in former Soviet and Eastern European countries. These findings show that uncertainty affects both the number and composition of trajectory clusters. Ignoring it risks over-interpreting unstable groups and overstating confidence in country classifications. Incorporating published uncertainty and measurement quality should become standard practice when clustering modelled health estimates.

papers.title: A Goal-Oriented Bayesian Experimental Design to Reduce Uncertainty in Sparse-Angle X-ray Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Sparse-angle X-ray computed tomography (CT) presents a challenge for reliable inference, as limited measurements may leave object boundaries unresolved. Bayesian optimal experimental design (BOED) methods select informative measurements, but can be computationally expensive or require data-driven surrogates and do not explicitly exploit microlocal visibility. We address this limitation by focusing on estimating inclusion boundaries rather than the entire attenuation field. For piecewise-constant objects, these boundaries correspond to singularities characterized by their wavefront sets. Microlocal analysis determines the X-ray view-angles at which these singularities are visible. We combine this information with Bayesian uncertainty quantification to introduce B-MUSE, a microlocal uncertainty-driven sequential experimental design method. We define a microlocal C-optimality criterion associated with the wavefront direction of the most uncertain boundary singularity and prove that its optimal solution satisfies the microlocal visibility condition. B-MUSE uses this result to sequentially select informative view-angles according to boundary uncertainty. It also incorporates an adaptive stopping criterion that terminates acquisition when additional measurements provide no meaningful uncertainty reduction. We evaluate B-MUSE through numerical experiments, including interpretable examples, prior-generated inclusions, and a multi-inclusion example from an external dataset, and benchmark it against recent methods. The results show that B-MUSE substantially reduces posterior uncertainty with few adaptively selected measurements while providing boundary estimates. These findings establish a direct connection between BOED and microlocal visibility and demonstrate the potential of uncertainty-driven acquisition to reduce measurement requirements for goal-oriented X-ray CT without training data.

papers.title: Credal Wrapper for Uncertainty Modelling in Sparse Geological Data
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for mineral exploration are trained on a few hundred sparse, expensive samples and used to decide where to drill next, so their epistemic uncertainty (EU), the part that more data could remove, matters as much as their predictions. Yet EU cannot be measured on real data, because the counterfactual that defines it is never observed, so estimators are graded by proxies such as out-of-distribution detection and calibration. We contribute a general simulation protocol that makes EU directly computable for a given model and can grade any EU estimator. It separates two estimands the literature conflates, reducible error and estimator spread, builds an oracle reference for each in a synthetic prospectivity field sampled by clustered drilling surveys, and compares uncertainty measures of an identical ensemble within each simulated world. We use it to ask when credal (imprecise-probability) measures are more faithful than Bayesian model averaging (BMA) in the sparse, low-class regime of geological classification. The credal interval width recovers the epistemic ordering better than BMA when members are few, confirming the small-ensemble advantage reported for credal wrappers; the advantage vanishes by M = 10 and reverses at M = 40. Secondly, the choice of credal functional matters more than the choice between credal and BMA. Lastly, the credal advantage does not widen as training data are thinned, so it compensates for few posterior samples rather than few data. On real drill-hole geochemistry from South Australia, a resampling oracle reproduces the first finding. The protocol applies to any EU estimator whose data-generating process can be simulated.

papers.title: Partial pooling beats synthetic respondents as estimators, not as covariates: a preregistered small-sample tournament
papers.abstract: Survey estimates for population segments, such as media use by sex and age, rest on few respondents per cell, and a growing literature offers synthetic respondents generated by large language models to fill the gap. That literature has not tested them against the small-area estimators a methodologist would otherwise use. We ran ten estimators, preregistered, on identical household-clustered splits of a Korean media panel across five calibration budgets and three holdout regimes. A multilevel partial-pooling model of the MRP family led every calibration-only estimator at every budget, matching at one hundred respondents what direct estimation reaches with roughly four times as many. On unobserved segments, information fixed as a per-segment prior was inert for synthetic panel and previous wave alike; attached as a bias correction it transferred, at the price of estimation noise. No registered synthetic advantage over MRP survived the paired decision rule. Entered instead as a covariate inside the multilevel model, an exploratory hybrid, the same panel improved on MRP on unobserved segments: the information survives where the registered constructions did not. Interval coverage stayed below nominal throughout and worsened with budget for partial pooling, contrary to prediction.

papers.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of automating end-to-end OpenFOAM workflows for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). However, current progress is bottlenecked by two critical limitations.
