Here we demonstrate a two-mode kinetic-inductance parametric amplifier based on a pair of capacitively coupled Kerr-nonlinear resonators fabricated from NbTiN and NbN thin films. The distributed Kerr nonlinearity of these materials enables nondegenerate four-wave-mixing amplification with gains approaching 40 dB, gain-bandwidth products up to 6.9 MHz, and 1-dB compression powers two to three orders of magnitude higher than those of state-of-the-art Josephson amplifiers. A coupled-mode theoretical model accurately captures the pump-induced modification of the hybridized modes and quantitatively reproduces the observed signal and idler responses. The NbN device exhibits a significantly larger Kerr coefficient and superior gain-bandwidth performance, highlighting the advantages of high-kinetic-inductance materials. Our results establish coupled kinetic-inductance resonators as a robust platform for broadband, high-power, and magnetically resilient quantum-limited amplification, offering a scalable route for advanced readout in superconducting qubits, spin ensembles, quantum dots, and other microwave-quantum technologies.

papers.title: Parametric Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Latent Routing of LoRA Adapters
papers.abstract: Parametric Retrieval-Augmented Generation (PRAG) is a RAG approach that integrates external knowledge directly into model parameters using a LoRA adapter, aiming at reducing the inference cost compared to traditional RAG. However, current PRAG approaches adopt a \textit{one-to-one} document encoding scheme, using a dedicated LoRA adapter for each individual document. This scheme introduces two major limitations: 1) As the number of documents increases, there will be a prohibitive cost for training and storage. 2) The LoRA adapters may largely overlap due to the shared knowledge across documents, making the approach highly inefficient. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Poly-PRAG approach, which uses a small set of LoRA adapters that are able to encode more general knowledge. Each document can be encoded using a combination of them through a latent routing function. By jointly training the LoRA adapters and the latent routing function, each LoRA adapter is able to encode a shared part of the knowledge across documents, and the routing function can select the best combination of adapters for a document. Experimental results on four benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the Poly-PRAG compared to other strong PRAG baselines. In addition, this approach reduces the storage requirement by avoiding the need to store a large number of LoRA adapters and offers a more efficient way to encode external knowledge into LLMs.

papers.title: Individualized Algorithmic Advice as a Strategic Signal on Competitive Markets
papers.abstract: As algorithms increasingly mediate competitive decision-making, their influence extends beyond individual outcomes to shaping strategic market dynamics. In our experiment, we examined how algorithmic advice affects human behavior in a classic economic game with a unique, non-collusive, and analytically traceable equilibrium. Participants (N = 129) played a Cournot quantity competition with equilibrium-aligned or strategically biased algorithmic recommendations. While individualized equilibrium advice supported stable convergence, collusively downward-biased advice led to sustained underproduction and supracompetitive profits - hallmarks of tacit collusion. Participants' quantities converged faster and more consistently toward individualized than collective equilibrium advice, potentially due to an objective quality advantage or greater perceived ownership of the former. These findings demonstrate that algorithmic advice can function as a strategic signal, shaping coordination even without explicit communication. The results echo real-world concerns about algorithmic collusion and underscore the need for careful design and oversight of algorithmic decision-support systems in competitive environments.

papers.title: Flow Reconstruction from Sparse Measurements in Urban Drainage Networks: A Simulation-Based Evaluation of Data-Driven Sparse Sensing
papers.abstract: Urbanization and increasingly frequent intense storms are placing stress on urban drainage networks. While dense monitoring is desirable, practical constraints in time, budget, and technology hinder its full implementation. How to monitor and predict flow conditions across the entire network under constrained resources is a major challenge. To address this, we evaluated data-driven sparse sensing (DSS), which selects sensor locations and reconstructs network-wide flow from the same reduced basis, in a 76-conduit urban drainage network. Simulations of a calibrated SWMM model were used to construct an event-weighted spatial basis using singular value decomposition (SVD), select rank-specific layouts using pivoted QR, and define the reconstruction decoder. Applied to 225 held-out simulations combining 25 plausible calibrated parameter sets with nine rainfall events, monitoring 5 of the 76 conduits (6.6%) achieved a median system-level Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.992 (10th percentile 0.973) for observed storms, and a median NSE of 0.967 at the active unmonitored conduits. Pivoted QR performed comparably to genetic-algorithm layouts without requiring iterative layout searches, whereas largest-upstream-area placement failed with the DSS decoder and trailed QR even with a weighted regression decoder. The DSS flow reconstruction performance was insensitive to prescribed multiplicative Gaussian measurement noise, additive noise up to about 2 L/s and a 10 L/s detection floor, but showed location-dependent responses to loss of a monitored conduit, which a refitted regression decoder largely removed. This study supports the use of DSS, driven by physics-based simulations, for deciding how many flow sensors to install and where.

papers.title: Maximal non-compactness of embeddings between sequence spaces
papers.abstract: We will focus on studying the ball measure of non-compactness $α(T)$ for various particular instances of embedding operators in sequence spaces. Our first main goal is to find necessary and sufficient conditions for an identity operator to be maximally non-compact. Next, we will focus on studying Lorentz sequence spaces $\ell^{p,q}$ and their basic properties. We will characterize the inclusions between Lorentz sequence spaces depending on the values of $p$ and $q$. Then we will try to determine exact values of the norms of the identity operators between these embedded spaces. Lastly, we will determine whether these identity operators are maximally non-compact by using our general theorems.

papers.title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
papers.abstract: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on our online science platform. It spans a diverse range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, modeling assumptions, redshifts, and numerical simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of weak absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.

papers.title: The Art of Asking: Multilingual Prompt Optimization for Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: Synthetic data has become a cornerstone for scaling LLMs, yet its benefits for multilingual modeling remain bottlenecked by translation. Translation for data augmentation inherits English-centric framing and style and neglects cultural dimensions, ultimately constraining model generalization. We argue that the overlooked prompt space offers a more powerful lever for improving multilingual performance. We introduce a lightweight framework for prompt-space optimization, where translated prompts are systematically transformed for Naturalness, Cultural Adaptation, and Difficulty Enhancement. Using an off-the-shelf multilingual LLM, we apply these transformations to prompts from 12 languages spanning 7 families. Under identical data conditions, our approach achieves substantial and consistent downstream improvements over the translation-only baseline: +4.7% accuracy on Global-MMLU, +2.4% XCometXL on Flores and +35.3% wins in preferences on mArenaHard. These gains are further corroborated by human preferences on open-ended creative writing. We establish prompt-space optimization as a simple yet powerful paradigm for building multilingual LLMs that are more robust, culturally grounded, and globally capable.

papers.title: A finite element method using a bounded auxiliary variable for solving the Richards equation
papers.abstract: The Richards equation, a nonlinear elliptic parabolic equation, is widely used to model infiltration in porous media. We develop a finite element method for solving the Richards equation by introducing a new bounded auxiliary variable to eliminate unbounded terms in the weak formulation of the method. This formulation is discretized using a semi-implicit scheme and the resulting nonlinear system is solved using Newton's method. Our approach eliminates the need of regularization techniques and offers advantages in handling both dry and fully saturated zones. In the proposed techniques, a non-overlapping Schwarz domain decomposition method is used for modeling infiltration in layered soils. We apply the proposed method to solve the Richards equation using the Havercamp and van Genuchten models for the capillary pressure. Numerical experiments are performed to validate the proposed approach, including tests such as modeling flows in fibrous sheets where the initial medium is totally dry, two cases with fully saturated and dry regions, and an infiltration problem in layered soils. The numerical results demonstrate the stability and accuracy of the proposed numerical method. The numerical solutions remain positive in the presence of totally dry zones. The numerical investigations clearly demonstrated the capability of the proposed method to effectively predict the dynamics of flows in unsaturated soils.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat's principle and Snell's law for cone structures and applications
papers.abstract: Fermat's principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures -- Lorentz-Finsler lightcones -- representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat's principle -- i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional -- its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell's law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo's navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.

papers.title: Berger-Joyal duality and traces I
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that the opposite of Joyal's disk category $\mathcal{D}_n$ is Berger's wreath product category $Θ_n = Δ\wr\cdots\wrΔ$. Our techniques continue to apply when the simplex category $Δ$ is replaced by Connes' cyclic category $Λ$ and some other crossed simplicial groups.

papers.title: A Computable Measure of Suboptimality for Entropy-Regularised Variational Objectives
papers.abstract: Several methods in statistics and machine learning target a probability distribution for which an entropy-regularised variational objective is minimised. This increased flexibility introduces a computational challenge, as one loses access to an explicit unnormalised density for the target. To mitigate this difficulty, we introduce a novel measure of suboptimality called 'gradient discrepancy', and in particular a kernel gradient discrepancy (KGD) that can be explicitly computed. In the Bayesian statistics context, KGD coincides with the kernel Stein discrepancy (KSD), and we obtain a novel characterisation of KSD as measuring the size of a variational gradient. Outside this familiar setting, KGD enables novel sampling algorithms to be developed and compared, even when unnormalised densities cannot be obtained. To illustrate this point several novel algorithms are proposed and studied, including a natural generalisation of Stein variational gradient descent, with applications to mean-field neural networks and predictively oriented posteriors presented. On the theoretical side, our principal contribution is to establish sufficient conditions for desirable properties of KGD, such as continuity and convergence control.

papers.title: When Graph Structure Provably Helps Classification: Non-Asymptotic Recovery Guarantees
papers.abstract: The joint use of graph structure and node-specific information is central to transductive node classification, yet a fundamental theoretical question remains: when does graph structure actually help? We provide the first deterministic, non-asymptotic, distribution-free answer to this question. We build on nuclear-norm graph clustering and generalized convex clustering. Our formulation of the latter incorporates node features, partial labels, and general convex loss functions, making it suitable for transductive node classification. We analyze each problem separately to characterize when graph structure alone, or node information alone, is sufficient for perfect recovery. We then formulate a unified convex optimization problem through a shared atomic norm representation and prove that combining the two sources expands the range of conditions under which perfect recovery is guaranteed beyond what either source alone can certify. This shows when node information can improve clustering and graph structure can improve classification.

papers.title: Re-evaluating Heart Rate Variability Biomarkers for Glucose Sensing: The Impact of Age Normalisation and Subject-Independent Validation
papers.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals may indicate glycemic status, but prior studies often combine distinct glucose targets and use validation strategies vulnerable to data leakage. Since HRV declines with age, aging may be confounded with diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction. We tested whether age-dependent HRV normalisation improves glycemic estimation. We analysed ECG features from 43 male patients with type 2 diabetes. Outcomes were glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c; n=29) and fasting blood glucose (FBG; n=38). We used leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, with feature selection and standardisation within each training fold. We compared 20 machine-learning algorithms, six age-adjustment methods, and 20 normalisation parameter combinations. Validation included 500 permutations and bootstrap confidence intervals. Extra Trees regression performed best: R2=0.222 (r=0.476, p=0.009) for HbA1c and R2=0.086 (r=0.344, p=0.034) for FBG. Mean absolute errors were 1.18 percentage points and 2.27 mmol/L, respectively. Permutation testing supported both associations (p=0.002). Contrary to our hypothesis, no age-adjustment method or parameter combination improved performance. Tree ensembles retained positive performance under strict validation, whereas linear models had negative R2 values; neural networks performed poorly. Strict within-fold preprocessing materially changed model performance and revealed potential inflation from conventional validation. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were [0.13, 0.82] for HbA1c R2 and [0.10, 0.72] for FBG R2. Although findings support HRV-glycemic associations, performance remains insufficient for standalone clinical use. The study highlights the importance of separating glycemic targets, subject-independent validation, within-fold preprocessing, and comprehensive baselines in non-invasive glycemic monitoring research.

papers.title: The limiting spectral distribution for sparse elliptic random matrices
papers.abstract: This paper studies sparse elliptic random matrix models which generalize both the classical elliptic ensembles and sparse i.i.d. matrix models by incorporating correlated entries and a tunable sparsity parameter $p_n$. Each $n\times n$ matrix $X_n$ is formed by entry-wise multiplication of an elliptic random matrix by an elliptic matrix of Bernoulli($p_n$) variables, where $np_n$ tends to infinity at a sufficient rate, allowing for interpolation between dense and sparse regimes. The main result establishes that after appropriate normalization, the empirical spectral measures of these matrices converge weakly in probability to the uniform measure on a rotated ellipsoid in the complex plane as the dimension $n$ tends to infinity. Interestingly, the shape of the limiting ellipsoid depends not only on the mirrored entry-wise correlation structure, but also non-trivially on the sparsity limit $p=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}p_n$.

papers.title: Simulating The Urban Canopy's Impact on Wind-Driven Natural Ventilation
papers.abstract: The urban canopy affects wind in complex ways, making it challenging to predict wind-driven natural ventilation and cooling in buildings. Using large eddy simulations of coupled outdoor and indoor airflow, we study how the surrounding urban canopy and wind angle influence ventilation rates through four ventilation configurations: cross, corner, dual-room, and single-sided. Flow visualizations demonstrate how both large-scale flow patterns and local interference effects can influence ventilation rates by 50-85%. In general, lower density canopies give higher ventilation rates and wind angles that align with a direct path between two openings also lead to higher ventilation rates. However, interference effects from surrounding buildings can significantly change the local wind speed and direction, thus also changing ventilation rates. The magnitude of these interference effects depends on both the wind angle and surrounding building geometries. The effect of wind angle is less pronounced in a higher density canopy, where the urban canopy geometry more strongly guides the flow. The results demonstrate that the canopy's effect on ventilation rates is much more complex than those suggested by existing natural ventilation parameterizations.

papers.title: Adversarial Observability and Performance Trade-offs in Optimal Control
papers.abstract: We develop a feedback controller that minimizes the observability of a set of adversarial sensors of a linear system, while adhering to strict closed-loop performance constraints. We quantify the effectiveness of adversarial sensors using the trace of their observability Gramian and its inverse, capturing both average observability and the least observable state directions of the system. We derive theoretical lower bounds on these metrics under performance constraints, characterizing the fundamental limits of observability reduction as a function of the performance trade-off. Finally, we show that the performance-constrained optimization of the Gramian's trace can be formulated as a one-shot semidefinite program, while we address the optimization of its inverse through sequential semidefinite programming. Aircraft and satellite simulations demonstrate that the proposed controllers reduce adversarial observability while maintaining near-optimal performance.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Probabilistic Dynamic-, Trajectory- and Vision-based Virtual Fixtures
papers.abstract: Probabilistic Virtual Fixtures (VFs) enable the adaptive selection of the most suitable haptic feedback for each phase of a task, based on learned or perceived uncertainty. While keeping the human in the loop remains essential, for instance, to ensure high precision, partial automation of certain task phases is critical for productivity. We present a unified framework for probabilistic VFs that seamlessly switches between manual fixtures, semi-automated fixtures (with the human handling precise tasks), and full autonomy. We introduce a novel probabilistic Dynamical System-based VF for coarse guidance, enabling the robot to autonomously complete certain task phases while keeping the human operator in the loop. For tasks requiring precise guidance, we extend probabilistic position-based trajectory fixtures with automation, allowing for seamless human interaction, geometry-awareness and optimal impedance gains. For manual tasks requiring very precise guidance, we also extend visual servoing fixtures with the same geometry-awareness and impedance behavior. We validate our approach on different robots, including an evaluation with expert users, showcasing operation modes, the ease of programming fixtures and lower interaction forces and favorable usability compared to a baseline.

papers.title: The N-Body Problem on Coadjoint Orbits
papers.abstract: We show (Theorem 3) that the symplectic reduction of the spatial $n$-body problem at non-zero angular momentum is a singular symplectic space consisting of two symplectic strata, one for spatial motions and the other for planar motions. Each stratum is realized as coadjoint orbit in the dual of the Lie algebra of the linear symplectic group $Sp(2n-2)$. The planar stratum arises as the frontier upon taking the closure of the spatial stratum. We reduce by going to center-of-mass coordinates to reduce by translations and boosts and then performing symplectic reduction with respect to the orthogonal group $O(3)$. The theorem is a special case of a general theorem (Theorem 2) which holds for the $n$-body problem in any dimension $d$. This theorem follows largely from a ``Poisson reduction'' theorem, Theorem 1. We achieve our reduction theorems by combining the Howe dual pair perspective of reduction espoused by Lerman-Montgomery-Sjamaar with a normal form arising from a symplectic singular value decomposition due to Xu. We begin the paper by showing how Poisson reduction by the Galilean group rewrites Newton's equations for the $n$-body problem as a Lax pair. In section 6.4 we show that this Lax pair representation of the $n$-body equations is equivalent to the Albouy-Chenciner representation in terms of symmetric matrices.

papers.title: HistogramTools for Efficient Data Analysis and Distribution Representation in Large Data Sets
papers.abstract: Histograms provide a powerful means of summarizing large data sets by representing their distribution in a compact, binned form. The HistogramTools R package enhances R built-in histogram functionality, offering advanced methods for manipulating and analyzing histograms, especially in large-scale data environments. Key features include the ability to serialize histograms using Protocol Buffers for distributed computing tasks, tools for merging and modifying histograms, and techniques for measuring and visualizing information loss in histogram representations. The package is particularly suited for environments utilizing MapReduce, where efficient storage and data sharing are critical. This paper presents various methods of histogram bin manipulation, distance measures, quantile approximation, and error estimation in cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) derived from histograms. Visualization techniques and efficient storage representations are also discussed alongside applications for large data processing and distributed computing tasks.

papers.title: Viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges to benchmark fluid simulations
papers.abstract: We present semi-analytical solutions for the evolution of both the temperature and chemical potentials for viscous Gubser flow with conserved charges. Such a solution can be especially useful in testing numerical codes intended to simulate relativistic fluids with large chemical potentials. The freeze-out hypersurface profiles for constant energy density are calculated, along with the corresponding normal vectors and presented as a new unit test for numerical codes. We also compare the influence of the equation of state on the semi-analytical solutions. We benchmark the newly developed Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code CCAKE that includes both shear viscosity and three conserved charges. The numerical solutions are in excellent agreement with the semi-analytical solution and also are able to accurately reproduce the hypersurface at freeze-out.

papers.title: Optimizing Bidding Curves for Renewable Energy in Two-Settlement Electricity Markets
papers.abstract: Coordination of day-ahead and real-time electricity markets is imperative for cost-effective electricity supply and also to provide efficient incentives for the energy transition. Although stochastic market designs feature the least-cost coordination, they are incompatible with current deterministic markets. This paper proposes a new approach for compatible coordination in two-settlement markets based on benchmark bidding curves for variable renewable energy. These curves are optimized based on a bilevel optimization problem, anticipating per-scenario responses of deterministic market-clearing problems and ultimately minimizing the expected cost across day-ahead and real-time markets. Although the general bilevel model is challenging to solve, we theoretically prove that a single-segment bidding curve with a zero bidding price is sufficient to achieve system optimality if the marginal cost of variable renewable energy is zero, thus addressing the computational challenge. In practice, variable renewable energy producers can be allowed to bid multi-segment curves with non-zero prices. We test the bilevel framework for both single- and multiple-segment bidding curves under the assumption of fixed bidding prices. We leverage duality theory and McCormick envelopes to derive the linear programming approximation of the bilevel problem, which scales to practical systems such as a 1576-bus NYISO system. We benchmark the proposed coordination and find absolute dominance over the baseline solution, which assumes that renewables agnostically bid their expected forecasts. We also demonstrate that our proposed scheme provides a good approximation of the least-cost, yet unattainable in practice, stochastic market outcome.

papers.title: Doubly Robust and Efficient Calibration of Prediction Sets for Right-Censored Time-to-Event Outcomes
papers.abstract: Our objective is to construct well-calibrated prediction sets for a time-to-event outcome subject to right-censoring with guaranteed coverage. Inspired by modern conformal inference, our approach avoids the need for a well-specified parametric or semiparametric survival model. Unlike existing conformal methods for survival data, which assume Type-I censoring with fully observed censoring times, we consider the more common right-censoring setting in which only the censoring time or only the event time is observed, whichever comes first. Under a standard conditional independence censoring condition, we propose and analyze several lower prediction bounds for the survival time of a future observation, including inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting, and its augmented version based on the semiparametric efficient influence function for the relevant marginal quantile of the outcome accounting for dependent censoring. We formally establish asymptotic coverage guarantees of the proposed methods, and demonstrate both theoretically and through empirical experiments, that the augmented approach substantially improves efficiency over all other proposed methods. Specifically, its coverage error bound is doubly robust, and therefore of second order, thus ensuring that it is asymptotically negligible relative to the coverage error of the other methods.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantified Deep Learning and Regression Analysis Framework for Image Segmentation of Skin Cancer Lesions
papers.abstract: Deep learning models (DLMs) frequently achieve accurate segmentation and classification of tumors from medical images. However, DLMs lacking feedback on their image segmentation mechanisms, such as Dice coefficients and confidence in their performance, face challenges when processing previously unseen images in real-world clinical settings. Uncertainty estimates to identify DLM predictions at the cellular or single-pixel level that require clinician review can enhance trust. However, their deployment requires significant computational resources. This study reports two DLMs, one trained from scratch and another based on transfer learning, with Monte Carlo dropout or Bayes-by-backprop uncertainty estimations to segment lesions from the publicly available The International Skin Imaging Collaboration-19 dermoscopy image database with cancerous lesions. A novel approach to compute pixel-by-pixel uncertainty estimations of DLM segmentation performance in multiple clinical regions from a single dermoscopy image with corresponding Dice scores is reported for the first time. Image-level uncertainty maps demonstrated correspondence between imperfect DLM segmentation and high uncertainty levels in specific skin tissue regions, with or without lesions. Four new linear regression models that can predict the Dice performance of DLM segmentation using constants and uncertainty measures, either individually or in combination from lesions, tissue structures, and non-tissue pixel regions critical for clinical diagnosis and prognostication in skin images (Spearman's correlation, p < 0.05), are reported for the first time for low-compute uncertainty estimation workflows.

papers.title: Toward Optimal-Complexity Hash-Based Asynchronous MVBA with Optimal Resilience
papers.abstract: Multi-valued validated Byzantine agreement (MVBA), a fundamental primitive of distributed computing, allows $n$ processes to agree on a valid $\ell$-bit value, despite $t$ faulty processes behaving maliciously. Among hash-based solutions for the asynchronous setting with adaptive faults, the state-of-the-art HMVBA protocol achieves optimal $O(n^2)$ message complexity, (near-)optimal $O(n \ell + n^2 λ\log n)$ bit complexity, and optimal $O(1)$ time complexity. However, it only tolerates $t < \frac15 n$ failures. In contrast, the best-known optimally-resilient protocol, SQ, incurs a higher bit complexity of $O(n^2 \ell + n^3 λ)$. This poses a fundamental question: Can a hash-based protocol be designed for the asynchronous setting with adaptive faults that simultaneously achieves optimal complexity and optimal resilience? This paper takes a significant step toward answering this question. Namely, we introduce Reducer, an MVBA protocol that retains HMVBA's optimal complexity while improving its resilience to $t < \frac14 n$. Like HMVBA and SQ, Reducer relies exclusively on collision-resistant hash functions. A key innovation in Reducer's design is its internal use of strong multi-valued Byzantine agreement (SMBA), a new variant of Byzantine agreement we introduce and construct, which ensures that the decided value was proposed by a correct process. To further advance resilience toward the optimal one-third bound, we then propose Reducer++, an MVBA protocol that tolerates up to $t < (\frac13 - ε)n$ adaptive failures, for any fixed constant $ε> 0$. Unlike Reducer, Reducer++ does not rely on SMBA. Instead, it employs a novel approach involving hash functions modeled as random oracles to ensure termination. Reducer++ maintains constant time complexity, quadratic message complexity, and quasi-quadratic bit complexity, with constants dependent on $ε$.

papers.title: Towards the Use of Anderson Acceleration in Coupled Transport-Gyrokinetic Turbulence Simulations
papers.abstract: Predicting the behavior of a magnetically confined fusion plasma over long time periods requires methods that can bridge the difference between transport and turbulent time scales. The nonlinear transport solver, Tango, enables simulations of very long times, in particular to steady state, by advancing each process independently with different time step sizes and couples them through a relaxed iteration scheme. We examine the use of Anderson Acceleration (AA) to reduce the total number of coupling iterations required by interfacing Tango with the AA implementation, including several extensions to AA, provided by the KINSOL nonlinear solver package in SUNDIALS. The ability to easily enable and adjust algorithmic options through KINSOL allows for rapid experimentation to evaluate different approaches with minimal effort. Additionally, we leverage the GPTune library to automate the optimization of algorithmic parameters within KINSOL. We show that AA can enable faster convergence in stiff and very stiff tests cases without noise present and in all cases, including with noisy fluxes, increases robustness and reduces sensitivity to the choice of relaxation strength.

papers.title: Euclidean Methods on Dirac Quantization and Gauge Representation
papers.abstract: Geometrical interpretation on U(1) gage theory of Dirac monopole, introduced here from the line integral\cite{Brandt} form of vector potentials, shows the gauge representation be multi-valued. In this paper, we construct Euclidean form of U(1) gauge theory on Dirac monopole based on the geometrical interpretation, derive the Dirac quantization condition geometrically. Even several theoretical methods which leads to Dirac quantization $eg=l/2$ has been developed, these are only possible under the postulate that gauge representation is single-valued. Using the line integration representation of vector potential, we derived the gauge equation which satisfies under the `phase gauge transformation' ($\mathbf{A}\to\mathbf{A}'=\mathbf{A}, \ ψ\toψ'=e^{ieΛ}ψ$), also showed that the Dirac quantization condition can be derived by the geometrical boundary condition on this gauge equation, without any supposing of canonical quantization condition. We finally explain geometrical meaning of constant phase of gauge and how the Dirac quantization holds single valued gauge representation.

papers.title: Asynchronous Decentralized Optimization with Constraints: Achievable Speeds of Convergence for Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: We address a decentralized convex optimization problem, where every agent has its unique local objective function and constraint set. Agents compute at different speeds, and their communication may be delayed and directed. For this setup, we propose an asynchronous double averaging and gradient projection (ASY-DAGP) algorithm. Our algorithm handles difficult scenarios such as message failure, by employing local buffers and utilizing the temporal correlation in the transmitted messages. We guarantee the convergence speed of our algorithm using performance estimation problems (PEP). In particular, we introduce the concept of the linear quadratic (LQ) PEP. This approach simplifies the analysis of smooth convex optimization problems, going beyond Lyapunov function analyses and avoiding restrictive assumptions such as strong-convexity. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm.

papers.title: Zero-divisor algebras of graph functions: quantum caging, entangling routing and stochastic first-passage exclusion
papers.abstract: We show how algebraic constraints on weighted graphs yield exact localization and controlled transport in quantum and stochastic systems. Antisymmetrizing a noncommutative, nonassociative product of vertex functions defines a Lie bracket. For a specified Lie cobracket over commutative rings without nonzero $2$-torsion, compatibility holds if and only if products of distinct incident edge weights vanish. When the coefficient ring is a finite product of integral domains, the edges with nonzero weights in each component of the ring form a matching. These matchings are determined by the edge weights and need not coincide across the components. These matchings yield exact two-vertex caging in fixed quantum channels; separately specified channel-selective controls enable coherent routing and path--internal-state entanglement. For matching-supported stochastic jump rates, they enforce first-passage exclusion, while prescribed internal-state switching opens inaccessible paths and yields a singular weak-switching escape limit. The bracket--cobracket factorization identifies a common edge operator underlying quantum kinetic Hamiltonians and Markov generators, subject to distinct sign and positivity conditions. The algebra fixes the channel structure; controlled motion requires additional dynamical operations.

papers.title: Local duality theorems for commutative algebraic groups
papers.abstract: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and let G be a commutative algebraic k-group that contains no nontrivial unipotent subgroups if car k=0. Given any presentation of G as an extension of commutative algebraic k-groups E: 0 --> L --> G --> A --> 0, where L is affine and A is an abelian variety, we establish Pontryagin duality theorems that relate the fppf cohomology groups of G (equipped with the extension structure E) to the hypercohomology groups of the dual of G in the truncated derived category D^{[-1,0]}(k_{fppf}). These results have applications (to be discussed elsewhere) to certain generalizations of Lichtenbaum-van Hamel duality to a class of non-smooth proper k-varieties.

papers.title: Finite Sample Inference in Incomplete Models
papers.abstract: We propose confidence regions for the parameters of incomplete models with exact coverage of the true parameter in finite samples. Our confidence region inverts a test, which generalizes Monte Carlo tests to incomplete models. The test statistic is a discrete analogue of a new optimal-transport formulation of the structural model. Both test statistic and critical values rely on simulation draws from the distribution of latent variables and are computed using solutions to discrete optimal transport, hence linear programming problems. We also propose a fast preliminary search in the parameter space with an alternative, more conservative yet consistent test, based on a parameter-free critical value. We show that this test is maximally consistent in the following sense: under infinite exchangeability, it consistently rejects every data-generating process that some test with finite-sample size control consistently rejects. We compare size and power of our procedure with competing proposals in simulations based on a regression with interval valued regressors. A second simulation based on latent consideration sets shows that dependent selection can severely distort inference calibrated under i.i.d. sampling, while our procedure retains finite-sample size control. Finally, we apply our methodology to the model of airline entry and price competition in Ciliberto et al. [2021].

papers.title: Deep Learning with Uncertainty Quantification for Predicting the Segmentation Dice Coefficient of Prostate Cancer Biopsy Images
papers.abstract: Deep learning models (DLMs) can achieve state-of-the-art performance in histopathology image segmentation and classification, but have limited deployment potential in real-world clinical settings. Uncertainty estimates of DLMs can increase trust by identifying predictions and images that need further review. Dice scores and coefficients (Dice) are benchmarks for evaluation of image segmentation performance, but are usually not evaluated with DLM uncertainty quantification. This study reports DLMs trained with uncertainty estimations, using randomly initialized weights and Monte Carlo dropout, to segment tumors from microscopic Hematoxylin and Eosin dye stained prostate core biopsy histology RGB images. Image-level maps showed significant correlation (Spearman's rank, p < 0.05) between overall and specific prostate tissue image sub-region uncertainties with model performance estimations by Dice. This study reports that linear models, which can predict Dice segmentation scores from multiple clinical sub-region-based uncertainties of prostate cancer, can serve as a more comprehensive performance evaluation metric without loss in predictive capability of DLMs, with a low root mean square error.

papers.title: Contrastive Semi-Supervised Segmentation with Class-wise Patches and Silhouette-Adaptive Consistency
papers.abstract: We present CSSL, a contrastive semi-supervised method for medical image segmentation. CSSL samples class-wise patches from labelled images and from confident pseudo-labels, separates their embeddings with a supervised contrastive loss with mixed hard negatives, and uses the Silhouette coefficient of the embedding clusters to set the strength of a feature-perturbation consistency loss. On MoNuSeg, patch embeddings are obtained by masked pooling of the encoder features of the unmasked image, nucleus rims form an additional contrastive class and a memory bank stores past embeddings; on CHAOS, patches are pixel-masked and no memory bank is used. The CSSL losses are added to a weak-to-strong pseudo-labelling recipe. We follow the protocols of published baselines: Self-Loop on MoNuSeg and DAFNet on CHAOS. On MoNuSeg with 50% labels, CSSL reaches 80.87 $\pm$ 0.17 nuclei F1 over three label splits, compared with 79.10 for Self-Loop and 78.73 for the same recipe without CSSL. On CHAOS T2 with 25% labels, CSSL reaches 89.01 Dice, compared with 82.0 for DAFNet and 88.94 for the recipe alone. Ablations show that the contrastive branch and, on MoNuSeg, the boundary class and feature-level pooling account for most of the improvement. Code: https://github.com/prinshul/CSSL

papers.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.

papers.title: A Semi-Analytic Approach To Valuing Auto-Callable Accrual Notes
papers.abstract: We develop a semi-analytic approach to the valuation of auto-callable structures with accrual features subject to barrier conditions. Our approach is based on recent studies of multi-assed binaries, present in the literature. We extend these studies to the case of time-dependent parameters. We compare numerically the semi-analytic approach and the day to day Monte Carlo approach and conclude that the semi-analytic approach is more advantageous for high precision valuation.

papers.title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
papers.abstract: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partialϕ)^4/Λ^4$ and $g_6(\partialϕ)^6/Λ^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

papers.title: Phase-Space Constraints on a General Class of Eckart-like Viscous Cosmologies
papers.abstract: We study the cosmological dynamics of a general class of viscous dark matter models using a dynamical system analysis. In the Eckart formalism, these viscous cosmologies are characterized by a dimensionless bulk viscous pressure $Ω_Π\equiv Ω_Π(Ω_m)$, where $Ω_m$ is the matter density parameter. Our analysis demonstrates that a viable early radiation era requires the complete absence of viscosity, a proper matter-dominated epoch demands a small viscous pressure, and the only physically admissible late-time attractor is the cosmological constant-dominated fixed point; consequently, the background expansion must closely track standard $Λ$CDM evolution. We validate these general results using the power-law parameterization $Ω_Π= -\hatξ_0 Ω_m^s$, where $\hatξ_0$ and $s$ are real parameters; for $s \geq 1$ and $\hatξ_0 \ll 1$, the model reproduces the $Λ$CDM background, while for $s < 1$ the system encounters a past-time integration boundary where the dark matter density transitions into negative values and its viscous pressure evaluates to nonphysical complex numbers. Since the background expansion essentially duplicates $Λ$CDM, the model is unlikely to resolve the $H_0$ tension. However, large differences arise at the linear perturbative level; indeed, on sub-horizon scales, bulk viscosity causes a scale-dependent dissipative drag on the matter density fluctuations; this increases the Hubble friction, offering a channel to suppress structure growth.

papers.title: Ballistic mixing: stellar mergers drive internal mixing in extremely massive stars, with implications for proto-globular cluster pollution
papers.abstract: Extremely massive stars, with masses of $10^3$-$10^4$ M$_\odot$, have been proposed as potential sources of the chemical enrichment associated with multiple populations in globular clusters. Early on the main sequence, these stars reach central temperatures of 65 to 75 MK, enabling nucleosynthesis through the CNO, NeNa, and MgAl cycles, producing abundance patterns similar to those observed in the so-called cluster's second population. Stellar mergers are among the leading formation channels for extremely massive stars. In this work, we follow the formation of a $\sim6700$ M$_\odot$ star via 253 stellar mergers, drawn from a direct $N$-body star cluster simulation with properties similar to the densest star clusters observed at redshift $z\sim10$. We evolve each star as a 1D stellar model and construct the merger products from mixing and shock heating prescriptions calibrated to 3D simulations of parabolic collisions. We find that entropy-based mixing efficiently transports nuclear-processed material from the convective core to the envelope, while merger-driven heating promotes chemical homogenization. As a result, the stellar surface becomes enriched with H-burning products, producing abundance patterns consistent with those observed in globular cluster multiple populations and supporting the role of merger-formed extremely massive stars as potential sources of early chemical enrichment in proto-globular cluster-like conditions.

papers.title: Reliable Estimation of Differential Privacy under Selection Bias
papers.abstract: Statistical privacy audits are essential for verifying the theoretical privacy guarantees of differentially private (DP) mechanisms. Auditors typically use Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) to estimate a lower bound on the true privacy leakage of DP mechanisms at a specified confidence level, which should not exceed the theoretical privacy upper bound guaranteed by DP. However, we found that many auditing implementations in prior work introduce a selection bias when running MIAs, which leads to statistically invalid and overestimated lower bounds. Because most audits are not tight, this bias has thus far gone unnoticed: the estimated lower bounds remained well below the theoretical upper bounds. Nevertheless, accurately evaluating this lower bound is critical, as a flawed statistical assessment could lead to false alarms on correct mechanisms or an incorrect evaluation of the guarantee's tightness. This work employs tools from the statistical literature to correct this bias. We present an overview of the different correction methods and assess their respective advantages. Furthermore, we perform a comprehensive re-analysis of results returned by prior audit implementations and show that without statistical correction, these audits violate the theoretical upper bounds up to four times more often than their claimed confidence level implies. With correction applied, the resulting lower bounds are statistically valid, and violations occur at no more than the nominal rate.

papers.title: HD 120678: a classical Be star with a tilting heartbeat disk
papers.abstract: Classical Oe/Be/Ae stars possess Keplerian circum-equatorial decretion disks which produce not just the eponymous emission lines but also the bewildering diversity of photometric variations on timescales above a few days. The variability is due to varying amounts and geometric distributions of the circumstellar gas. The ASAS-3 V-band light curve of HD 120678 between March 2005 and November 2008 resembled an inverse P Cygni profile, which may have been a one-off event. The peak-to-valley amplitude reached ~0.9 mag. Before and after this photometric event, the Balmer emission lines and their variability matched those of classical Be stars with an intermediate to low inclination angle. At the sharp minimum of the light curve, Gamen et al. (2012) observed shell-type profiles implying an edge-on (high-inclination) view. For the historical activity phases of gamma Cas and 59 Cyg, such a Be => Be-shell => Be sequence has been successfully interpreted as rotations of the disk plane. HD 120678 and a few other Be stars add a not previously recognized phenomenon to the plethora of Be-star variabilities, namely heartbeat light curves. Analogously to the distortion of heartbeat stars, the variability is due to heartbeat disks gravitationally tilted by an additional star as modeled by Marr et al. (2022) for Pleione. While the typical amplitudes of heartbeat stars are only a few 0.01 mag, heartbeat disks can explain the ten times larger amplitudes observed in Be stars.

papers.title: Evidence for Suppressed Non-thermal Broadening in a Flare Ribbon from Stereoscopic Observations
papers.abstract: Flare ribbons mark the footpoints of newly reconnected magnetic loops and are commonly associated with strong plasma flows and enhanced non-thermal broadening of transition-region lines due to impulsive energy deposition. However, the mechanisms governing energy transport into flare ribbons remain uncertain, particularly under different magnetic field configurations. We investigate the energy deposition process at a flare ribbon near a sunspot by determining the physical nature of its small-scale downflows. We study small-scale downflows in a remote ribbon during the M7.7-class event on 30 September 2024, using coordinated observations from SDO, IRIS, and Solar Orbiter. We use stereoscopic imaging from Solar Orbiter and IRIS to detect plane-of-sky motions on small scales (200 km). We conduct spectroscopic analysis of IRIS Si IV profiles, complemented by C II and Mg II diagnostics. Apparent downflow speeds measured from Solar Orbiter imaging (limb view) are 85-130 km/s, while IRIS images (disk view) reveal plane-of-sky speeds of 70-85 km/s. In contrast, IRIS Si IV profiles at the brightest ribbon pixels are well approximated by a single Gaussian, with minimal Doppler shifts and unexpectedly small non-thermal widths (10 km/s). Peak Si IV emission also coincides with a deeper Mg II central reversal, while electron densities are one to two orders of magnitude higher than typical quiet-Sun values. The absence of significant line-of-sight velocities and non-thermal broadening differs from typical flare-ribbon behavior. Our results are consistent with a scenario in which plasma motions are guided by highly inclined (nearly horizontal) magnetic fields in chromospheric canopy and are not accompanied by strong turbulence or wave motions. This study suggests that flare ribbons can exhibit a wide diversity of lower-atmospheric responses and emphasizes the critical role of magnetic field geometry.

papers.title: The compact jets of the black hole X-ray binary Swift J1753.5-0127 during its 2023-2024 outburst
papers.abstract: X-ray binaries are excellent laboratories to study the coupling between accretion and ejection phenomena around compact objects through multiwavelength observations. Swift J1753.5-0127 is a black hole low-mass X-ray binary discovered in outburst in 2005 that remained active for 11 years, followed by two mini-outbursts. We investigate the behavior of the compact jets of Swift J1753.5-0127 during its 2023-2024 outburst. We report a dense multiwavelength monitoring in the radio, NIR/optical/UV and X-ray bands. Using new and archival luminosity measurements, we construct a refined, smoother radio/X-ray plane that covers the steep/outlier and shallow/transition branches of the radio/X-ray correlation. We also present spectral energy distributions (SEDs) constructed using quasi-simultaneous observations from four epochs. Swift J1753.5-0127 underwent a faint, hard-only, double-peaked outburst, followed by a re-brightening in the optical. The updated radio/X-ray plane offers a clear view on the region occupied by this source, similar to MAXI J1348-630, but at lower radio luminosities than H 1743-322, and we confirm its hybrid behavior. The broad-band SED fitting reveals that a cool, truncated accretion disk dominates the NIR/optical/UV band. We find that the compact jets have a variable but weak contribution in the NIR, with a break frequency $ν_\mathrm{break} \lesssim 5 \times 10^{12}~\mathrm{Hz}$, providing additional evidence that radio-quiet sources are also infrared-quiet. We also find evidence that the radio spectral index evolves with X-ray luminosity, transitioning from inverted values near quiescence to flatter or negative values at higher luminosities. In the context of adiabatic jet models, this trend may indicate that the jet geometry becomes increasingly confined as the accretion rate rises.

papers.title: Delving into the depths of NGC 3783 with XRISM VI. Evidence for a failed wind based on Fe xxv absorption line variability
papers.abstract: NGC 3783 exhibits a prominent Fe XXV absorption trough in the time-averaged XRISM/Resolve spectrum. To investigate its short-term variability, we present a time-resolved analysis of the Fe XXV absorption line during the continuous 10-day observation. We divided the resolved absorption profile into five fixed velocity intervals and measured their normalized equivalent widths in 19 time-resolved spectra. Three velocity intervals exhibit significant equivalent-width (EW) variability. Two velocity intervals respond differently to low- and high-flux states with less emission line contamination. The time-dependent photoionisation modelling is unable to reproduce the most significant observed EW variation ($3.5 \, σ$), possibly owing to uncertainties in the assumed initial equilibrium state, which prevent a precise density measurement. Instead, using photoionisation calculations and assuming the high-density limit, we derive approximate constraints on the ionisation parameters of the two relevant components. The low-velocity component (-320 to -680 km/s) shows a delayed inverse response, indicating a high ionisation parameter, while its relatively short lag timescale indicates a relatively high density and a distance upper limit of 0.05 pc. In contrast, the high-velocity component (-680 to -1040 km/s) manifests a positive response with a longer lag to the ionising continuum, implying a relatively low ionisation parameter. This component appears to be less dense, with an inferred distance upper limit of 0.25 pc. The low-velocity component is consistent with a failed wind, as its outflow velocity is below the local escape velocity, whereas the high-velocity component lies near the escape threshold. Together with the lower-ionisation failed wind detected in 2001, this supports a multiphase failed-wind scenario in the unobscured state of NGC~3783 over more than two decades.

papers.title: MATISSE unveils a dusty disc in the interior of EP Aquarii. First evidence of a misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star?
papers.abstract: Aims. We have mapped the dust and molecular gas emission distributions in the vicinity (a few stellar radii) of the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star EP\,Aquarii, with a previously reported stellar companion at $\sim$50\,au, to search for binary-induced asymmetries. Methods. We present an analysis of new high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$4\,mas) images obtained with MATISSE (in the wavelength range $\sim$3--8\,\mum) as well as archival high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$20\,mas) ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,(c$J$=2-1) line and continuum emission observations ($\sim$230\,GHz), to study the circumstellar morphology and kinematics of the molecular gas on these spatial scales. Results. The MATISSE images display a bright central source and two slightly extended emission features ("blobs") located on opposite sides of the AGB star (at radial distances of $\sim$4--10\,au). These structures are consistent with previous mid-infrared interferometric observations, suggesting stability over decades. The central source is elongated along the direction defined by the blobs, in both the MATISSE and ALMA continuum images. The ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,($J$=2-1) maps display an asymmetric inner wind with a velocity gradient. Conclusions. The observations are consistent with an edge-on dusty equatorial overdensity (disc-like), hinting the presence of a close ($\lesssim$4\,au) companion. The inferred symmetry axis is almost perpendicular to the CO velocity gradient and the orbital plane proposed for the distant ($\sim$50\,au) companion. EP\,Aqr may represent the first misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star.

papers.title: High-resolution transmission spectroscopy of KELT-18b Metastable helium detection at 1083 nm
papers.abstract: We present the first high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of the ultrahot Jupiter KELT-18b, probing its escaping atmosphere by analyzing a single transit obtained with the CARMENES spectrograph. Transmission spectroscopy and Doppler tomography were utilized to isolate the planetary signal. To mitigate contamination from the strong telluric OH lines overlapping the region of interest, two distinct data analysis procedures were applied: a standard Molecfit and OH-masking approach as well as a PCA-based method. By combining the two complementary approaches, we successfully detect a He\,I triplet absorption feature of $1.10 \pm 0.22\%$ ($5.1σ$). The signal exhibits a velocity shift consistent with zero and is attributed to the exoplanetary atmosphere. An injection test reveals that the PCA-based method significantly suppresses the retrieved signal. Additionally, using the ATES and TPM codes, we modeled the atmospheric photoevaporation and the helium triplet profile for different He/H ratios and stellar XUV fluxes, accounting for instrument and planetary rotational broadening. From our simulations we derive a mass-loss rate and an evaporation efficiency for KELT-18b of $10.47 \leq \log_{10}(\dot{M}) \leq 11.68$ and $0.153 \leq η\leq 0.321$, demonstrating that the atmosphere of KELT-18b is undergoing photoevaporation. Furthermore, our simulations show good agreement with the observed transmission spectrum, allowing us to exclude very low He/H ratios at a $3σ$ confidence level for XUV fluxes up to approximately twice the nominal reconstructed value. Our result expands the known parameter space of exoplanets with confirmed helium absorption, establishing KELT-18b as the most massive planet orbiting the hottest host star with such a detection.

papers.title: Interaction of eccentricity tide and convection
papers.abstract: Aim. We try to understand the interaction of eccentricity tide and convection in icy satellites. Method. We use the numerical calculation of rotating convection with eccentricity tide in a spherical shell. Results. We have the following results. (1) Energy scaling exponent about buoyancy force (or tidal force) decreases with increasing tidal force (or buoyancy force). (2) The combined tide-convection flow is not identical to superposition of two pure flows in respect of energy spectrum. (3) Tide controls large-scale of fluid motion but convection is important for small scale, and the mode-mode transition occurs at intermediate scales. (4) Tide suppresses heat transport efficiency. (5) Dissipation of kinetic energy scales as square of tidal force with a very weak dependence on buoyancy force, which has little impact on dissipation but suppresses the tidal influence on dissipation.

papers.title: Insights from the stability of methanol maser flare properties I: G9.62+0.20E
papers.abstract: The brightest 6.7 GHz methanol maser in the Galaxy is associated with the high-mass star-forming region (HMSFR) G009.62+0.20E. Additionally, this methanol maser shows periodic flaring observed at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Several models have been hypothesized to explain the periodicity, including periodic accretion, spiral shocks in the gaps of circumbinary disks, pulsating stars, dicke's superradiance, and a colliding wind binary (CWB) system. We analyzed the time series of the 1.22 km s-1 feature of the 6.7 GHz methanol maser spectrum and the 1.25 km s-1 feature of the 12.2 GHz methanol maser spectrum over the monitoring duration of roughly 20 years, to determine an updated period, analyze the stability and repeatability of the flares, the temporal behavior of the flare profile, and the duty cycle of the flare profile based on the updated period. From these results, it is argued for or against any of the mechanisms that have been proposed to explain the periodicity. Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods were used to determine the methanol maser period at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Once the period has been determined, phase-folding or period-folding was used to analyze the flare shape, flare stability, and duty cycle of the flares. The periods of the 6.7 and 12.2 GHz methanol masers were determined to be ~ 243.0 +- 0.3 days. The flares are highly repeatable, stable, and show almost identical shapes, as well as their duty cycles. A replicated kernel density estimator (KDE) of the flare shape reproduces the time series very well over a time span of ~ 8000 days. After careful consideration of the proposed mechanisms for periodic methanol masers, we conclude that all but one, the CWB model, have been ruled out as a possible driver of this flare profile. It has also been established that the CWB model can qualitatively explain the flare profile of the periodic methanol masers.

papers.title: The origin of the high heavy-element content of warm Jupiters
papers.abstract: Planet interior models have revealed that warm Jupiters should harbor large heavy element masses (up to 30-40% of the planetary mass). Within the pebble drift and evaporation scenario, inward drifting pebbles can evaporate and enrich the inner disc with vapor to super-stellar values, accreteable by giant planets. As H$_2$O ice evaporates in the inner disc, while CO$_2$, CH$_4$ and CO evaporate in the outer disc, the enrichment of the disc with vapor decreases with increasing orbital distance. We use the chemcomp code to model the migration and growth of planets via pebble and gas accretion in discs around stars with different masses and discs with different sizes. We show (i) that pebble drift and evaporation can explain the wide range of derived heavy element contents of giant planets. (ii) Giant planets forming around stars with larger disc sizes can accrete larger quantities of heavy elements, because these discs can maintain a high pebble flux for a longer time. (iii) Planets forming or migrating interior to the water ice line can accrete larger amounts of heavy elements via the accretion of vapor enriched gas compared to planets forming in the outer disc regions. (iv) Metal rich stars can allow the formation of planets that are more enriched in heavy elements, if they form in the inner disc regions. Planets forming in the outer disc regions will be - independently of the disc metallicity - much less enriched compared. (v) Planets forming in discs with the same size and total mass, but around stars with higher mass, are only marginally more enriched compared to their counterparts forming around lower mass star. Our study suggests that the trend of increasing total heavy element mass with increasing planetary mass is caused by the accretion of vapor enriched gas in discs with different sizes in the combination with different origins of warm giant planets from the inner and outer disc.

papers.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: a benchmark K-dwarf with a compact planetary system
papers.abstract: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency. We advocate adopting the asteroseismic radius, which is robust to modeling assumptions and optimisation strategies.

papers.title: Formation Dynamics of a Rotating Solar Spicule-like Event and Associated Energy-Mass Transport
papers.abstract: We performed three-dimensional radiative magnetohydrodynamic(3D RMHD) simulations in an upward-directed (positive-polarity) open magnetic field with an initial background strength of 10 G. We identified vortex-associated spicule-like events and carried out a detailed analysis of one representative event. Prior to the formation of this spicule-like event, a photospheric vortex appears and twists the magnetic field lines, then develops upward into higher atmospheric layers, forming a magnetic tornado system. This event is generated during this process. At the periphery of this magnetic tornado, twisted magnetic field lines with negative vertical components reconnect with both external positive-polarity background fields and central positive-polarity fields. The magnetic reconnection sites rise and rotate together with the developed magnetic tornado, and many jet-like substructures in this event are closely associated with plasma upward ejections from these reconnection regions. A vertical force analysis shows that, for this event, plasma uplift in the photosphere and lower chromosphere is dominated by the pressure-gradient force, whereas in the upper chromosphere, the Lorentz force gradually becomes dominant. At a height of about 4 Mm above the solar surface, this event produces a mean upward mass flux density on the order of $10^{-7}~{\rm kg~m^{-2}~s^{-1}}$ and a mean upward Poynting flux density of approximately $525~{\rm W~m^{-2}}$. The wave-mode decomposition results show that the energy transport associated with the rotational spicule-like event is dominated by the Alfvén mode. Alfvén waves, fast-mode waves, and slow-mode waves carry energy into the lower corona in an approximate ratio of $10:7:3$.

papers.title: Star Cluster Ecology VIII. -- Dynamically Forming S-Type and $α$Centauri-like Systems
papers.abstract: Aims: To analyse the impact of dynamically formed binaries emerging naturally from various star cluster environments on already established planetary systems. Methods: Numerical simulations replicating the star-forming region NGC 1333 are conducted. We consider three models, each using identical cluster realisations and simulation parameters. The cluster itself is initially sub-virial and fractally distributed. Model~A assumes planetary systems are initially in mean motion resonance. In Model~B, the same planetary systems are moved out of resonance, but remain intrinsically stable. Finally, Model~C removes all planets from the simulation. Ten independent realisations are integrated per model until 30 Myr. Results: Dynamically formed binaries emerge at similar rates across models, indicating planets play little role in their formation. We also find a higher production rate of wide binaries compared to previous numerical studies which we attribute to the sub-virial and sub-clustered initial conditions. S-type and binary S-type planetary systems naturally emerge in our simulations, while P-type systems are rare. For Model~A, the fraction of S-type or binary S-type systems is f_{\rm S}=0.02 and $f_{\rm Bin,\, S}=0.05, respectively. Rogue planets originating from a binary system are ejected with a substantially larger velocity than those around singletons. Planet-star collisions and planet capture events occur disproportionately within binary systems. Finally, several \alphaCentauri-like systems emerge in our simulations, suggesting that the nearest stellar system to the Sun may have a dynamical origin.

papers.title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
papers.abstract: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$α$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$α$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.

papers.title: Gen-EBM: an energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
papers.abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that depend sensitively on climate feedbacks. We introduce the Geneva Energy Balance Model (Gen-EBM), a new 1-D latitudinal EBM for rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. Gen-EBM is implemented in Rust and builds on previous exoplanet EBMs by incorporating a temperature-dependent outgoing longwave radiation prescription spanning Earth-like, runaway-onset, and post-runaway greenhouse regimes. We construct bifurcation diagrams from ensembles of simulations and explore the effects of rotation rate, orbital eccentricity under the mean-flux approximation, and surface thermal inertia. Including post-runaway greenhouse states substantially enlarges the parameter space over which multiple climate states coexist. Within our model framework, slow rotators approach the spatially homogeneous limit and maintain broader temperate stability ranges, whereas fast rotators develop strong equator-to-pole temperature gradients that narrow the temperate branch. Under the mean-flux approximation, increasing eccentricity enhances climate variability and can alter the attractor structure itself. The critical eccentricity at which temperate climates disappear depends strongly on thermal inertia, with ocean-rich planets remaining stable to larger eccentricities than land-dominated planets. Gen-EBM therefore broadens rapid parameter-space exploration to climates spanning temperate, runaway-onset, and post-runaway regimes. Its computational efficiency and flexibility make it a valuable bridge between simple climate models and 3-D general circulation models.

papers.title: EK Cha b: multi-tracer detection of a protoplanet candidate in a gas-rich environment
papers.abstract: Despite sustained community efforts and advances in instrumentation and high-contrast imaging, the search for protoplanets remains difficult, with only two widely accepted systems to date in Class II systems (PDS 70 and WISPIT 2). Here we present the detection of EK Cha b, a new protoplanet candidate, identified through CO emission, millimeter continuum and 0.82 micron broadband photometry, linked to EK Cha, a young late-type M star. The detection of a new protoplanet candidate offers an additional opportunity to advance our understanding of planet formation. By exploiting the wealth of archival data available for nearby star-forming regions, we aim to place EK Cha b in context, characterize its properties, and motivate future campaigns targeting similar systems. We analyzed high-spatial-resolution archival observations of EK Cha from HST, VLT/NACO, VLT/MUSE, and ALMA. We searched for EK Cha b in broadband continuum and gas tracers, reporting the measured flux with uncertainties, and upper limits for non-detections. EK Cha b shows a spectrally-resolved footprint that matches the CO J=2--1 emission, together with 0.82 micron and millimeter continuum emission. EK Cha b is spectrally resolved in CO J=2--1 emission, kinematically consistent with a circumplanetary disk. Best fits from evolutionary models place EK Cha b as a planetary mass companion, although deeper observations are required to fully confirm its nature. Although giant planets are uncommon around M dwarfs, these stars host the highest planet occurrence rate while remaining severely underrepresented in protoplanet searches. EK Cha b demonstrates that such systems are now within reach, and the advent of extremely large telescopes and improved high-contrast imaging -- where the lower host luminosity relaxes the required contras-- will open this overlooked regime to systematic exploration.

papers.title: A "universal" supernova efficiency to drive the HI turbulence in nearby star-forming galaxies
papers.abstract: The origin of cold gas turbulence in galaxies has long been debated. Supernovae (SNe), the dominant form of stellar feedback, were thought insufficient to sustain it against dissipation, especially in galactic environments with low star formation rates (SFRs). We investigate the origin of the neutral atomic gas (HI) turbulence in dwarf irregular galaxies, a challenging regime of low masses and SFRs. We build on a recent study of spirals showing that disc flaring prolongs the dissipation timescale, reducing the energy needed to sustain turbulence and making SN feedback viable. We measure the SN efficiency, that is the fraction of SN energy required to sustain HI turbulence, in 14 dwarfs, and test whether a "universal" efficiency holds across a sample representative of the star-forming main sequence. From the observed HI distributions and kinematics, we derive the radial profiles of the HI kinetic energy per unit area and model them as the sum of thermal energy and turbulent energy from SNe, constrained by the observed SFR surface density. We consider pure cold and warm neutral medium (WNM) phases as limiting cases, as well as a mixed two-phase scenario, obtaining the SN efficiency and WNM fraction via hierarchical Bayesian inference. We find that the observed HI kinetic energy in dwarfs requires only $\lesssim 3\%$ of the SN energy, and that a "universal" efficiency of $\approx 2\%$ explains the HI turbulence across our main-sequence sample. Our findings suggest that the SN efficiency remains similar across galaxies with different properties, offering valuable constraint for feedback recipes in galaxy evolution models.

papers.title: Light curve spectral energy distribution fitting of 13 carbon-rich Mira variables stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: Carbon-rich Mira variables are highly dynamic stars characterized by large-amplitude radial pulsations and intense mass-loss.
