Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. Taken together, the results indicate that visual prompting primarily aids KGQA by enhancing prediction precision in low-complexity contexts, provided that visual design respects cognitive and perceptual constraints. To optimize both accuracy and inference efficiency, we argue for adaptive visual prompting policies that selectively append diagrams to small, visually sparse subgraphs with well-structured layouts, avoiding unnecessary visual clutter and token overhead on complex queries. We conclude by relating these findings to a visual notation design theory, outlining how principled diagram encoding can guide future multimodal VLM prompting.

papers.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. Contrastive direction analysis finds geometry aligned with the human matrix in larger instruct variants, but little alignment in base variants under this assay. Across models, geometry strength is associated with behavioral amplification (r = 0.68, p = 0.008; partial r = 0.69 controlling for log size). To relate internal structure to output behavior, a matched activation-probing paradigm shows that probe slopes vary less than behavioral slopes (1.38-1.77 vs 0.52-1.53). A synthetic control shows that ridge probing can inflate these slopes; after subtracting a baseline based on a reliability proxy from another analysis, adjusted slopes remain associated with behavior (r = 0.88). We term the measured probe-behavior gap readout attenuation. These results establish decodability and geometric alignment under the tested assays, without showing that the measured directions mediate the cross-persona answers.

papers.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
papers.abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. To support training and evaluation in this domain, we also present LandslideVL, the first benchmark for intelligent landslide analysis, combining visual imagery and newly introduced textual prompts. Comprehensive experiments across public datasets and LandslideVL demonstrate that LandslideFM achieves superior quantitative and qualitative performance. Most importantly, LandslideFM surpasses general-purpose VLMs in specialized landslide reasoning and scene analysis. Our code is released at https://github.com/wangshanwen001/LandslideFM.

papers.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
papers.abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mercity-AI/SAE-Guardrails and https://huggingface.co/collections/Mercity/online-guardrails-using-sparse-autoencoders-6ac602940468c62fefb2b9e8

papers.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
papers.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.

papers.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
papers.abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.

papers.title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
papers.abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.

papers.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
papers.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(Λ)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $Λ$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(Λ)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $Λ$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

papers.title: Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning for CAD Decomposition toward All-Hexahedral Meshing
papers.abstract: Automatic hexahedral meshing for complex CAD models has long been regarded as the "holy grail" of mesh generation. The fundamental challenge arises from feature misalignment, where orthogonal or interacting features coexist, making direct hexahedral meshing infeasible and requiring decomposition into simpler, meshable blocks. While existing decomposition methods, including frame-field pipelines and learning-based techniques, have reduced manual intervention, they can remain sensitive to geometric and topological complexity and may fail to produce valid decompositions for challenging feature configurations. Specifically, their action spaces are typically restricted to surface-based splitting, which often yields invalid or unmeshable decompositions. To address these limitations, we propose DecompRL, a deep reinforcement learning framework for CAD decomposition toward hexahedral meshing. We design a set of topology-aware internal-splitting actions that leverage both global topological structure and local geometric property to effectively separate misaligned features. Furthermore, we introduce geometric rewards together with meshability feedback to guide the learning process toward valid decompositions and high-quality meshes. Extensive experiments on ABC, Fusion360, NIST, and DeepCAD show that DecompRL achieves the highest success rate among the evaluated learning-based methods on three of the four benchmarks, while maintaining competitive mesh quality. The measured LMFF-to-DecompRL runtime ratio reaches up to two orders of magnitude; this compares the full LMFF procedure with DecompRL decomposition alone, excluding subsequent mesh generation. The largest SR improvement is observed on Fusion360, where DecompRL reaches a success rate of 59.6%.

papers.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
papers.abstract: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $Δ(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior. Under natural nondegeneracy assumptions, $I(t)\to0$, $V(t)\to0$, $H(t)\to H_\infty>0$, and $D(t)\to D_\infty$. We also derive peak conditions, a final-size identity, and discuss the biological interpretation of $\mathfrak{a}$ as a dynamical responsiveness or short-memory parameter.

papers.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission
papers.abstract: Video applications are increasingly prevalent, yet their high data volume and temporal dependency make robust wireless transmission challenging under limited communication resources. To address this issue, we propose a token importance-aware semantic communication (Ti-SemCom) framework for bandwidth-efficient video transmission. Specifically, object and motion information is jointly extracted to identify communication-relevant regions, which are hierarchically associated with semantic tokens according to their importance. The transmitted tokens are then dynamically selected based on both token importance and the available bandwidth, prioritizing more informative video content under resource constraints. At the receiver, untransmitted regions reuse recently reconstructed references to further reduce redundant transmission. Experiments on the CAVIAR dataset show that Ti-SemCom can achieve an 88.3\% reduction in communication cost while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality.

papers.title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
papers.abstract: Assisted history matching remains non-unique because many geological realisations can reproduce equivalent production responses with substantial differences between individual well matches. This ambiguity increases when a field comprises several depositional settings and modelling strategies. The paper applied a graph autoencoder approach to history matching of a benchmark Brugge field that comprises different depositional zones. Each stratigraphic zone is modelled with its dedicated generative model that comprises a joint latent space for optimisation history matching loops. Graph-based generators operate directly on the active cells of the corner-point grid, so its irregular geometry is handled without conversion to a regular lattice. The optimisation search in the 160-dimensional joint latent space is done with the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy. The multi-component objective function includes static well data mismatch, dynamic production mismatch, and a geological realism penalty based on the Decoder induced latent metric. Latent space diagnostics with topological data analysis are applied prior to history matching to test whether one generator is sufficient or whether a multiple generator formulation is required. The results show that the zone-based formulation gives coherent latent spaces, preserves the main porosity and permeability relations that vary from one zone to another, and supports history matching while keeping the solutions within the learned geological manifold. The matched models reproduce field oil and water production within the prior uncertainty range and provide a comparable well-level match to previously published Brugge studies based on Ensemble Kalman Filter, Particle Swarm Optimisation with principal component analysis of parameterisation, and Multiple Kernel Learning with Particle Swarm Optimisation.

papers.title: marineGeochemFoam: A multipurpose framework for simulating reactive transport and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and at seawater-groundwater interfaces
papers.abstract: We present marineGeochemFoam, an open-source reactive transport modeling framework for simulating early diagenesis, sediment burial, submarine groundwater discharge, and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and groundwater-seawater transition zones. The code is implemented in the widely used numerical toolbox OpenFOAM and extends the capabilities of the existing diagenetic models by supporting, among other features, i) coupled reactive transport of dissolved solute and solid species, (ii) a flexible native reaction package, supporting arbitrary reaction networks with n-th order and Monod-type kinetics, and (iii) coupling with an external geochemical code, PHREEEQC, providing access to a wide range of thermodynamically based geochemical processes. We benchmarked different features of the code across various examples with increasing complexity. Successively, the code was applied to two case studies reproducing field observations from the Hanko groundwater discharge site, Finland, and the Santa Barbara Basin, California. Beyond diagenetic applications, the code also serves as a general-purpose reactive transport simulator.

papers.title: Two-Sided Amortized Resource Analysis: Verifying Resource Lower Bounds via Ill-Typing
papers.abstract: We present a two-sided type system with potential for verifying resource lower bounds of functional programs. Automatic amortized resource analysis (AARA) verifies upper bounds: types carry potential, and typing certifies sufficient resources. A lower bound, however, is a necessity statement---the program evaluates only if enough resources are available---and prior type-based approaches obtain it by switching the substructural discipline of potential, so that upper and lower bounds live in separate type systems. Matching upper and lower bounds characterize a program's cost exactly. Our system combines AARA-style potential with the two-sided type systems of Ramsay and Walpole, whose central guarantee is that ill-typed programs do not evaluate. Typing formulas may constrain arbitrary terms and appear on both sides of the turnstile; the judgment $t : A \vdash q$ states that if $t$ evaluates to a result of type $A$, then at least $q$ units of resource must be available---that is, $q$ is a lower bound. Because potential makes typing formulas non-replicable, our system follows an affine discipline instead of the replicable contexts of the original framework. We interpret types by semantic typing over value states, pairs of values and remaining resources, and we prove soundness on a safety fragment; corollaries recover the classical two-sided guarantees and the soundness of both kinds of bounds in a single proof system. A prototype type checker in OCaml verifies, on a suite of 19 benchmarks, matching pairs of bounds that characterize costs exactly, as well as lower bounds for programs whose upper bounds are unavailable. In a parallel exploration, we study a two-sided linear type system in which every value is a non-replicable resource; there, closures that capture linear resources call for dual typing formulas, and the exact accounting explains the affine design of the main system.

papers.title: Conformally Sasakian manifolds and the $k$-nullity condition
papers.abstract: We study almost contact metric manifolds that are locally conformal to Sasakian manifolds in the normalization of Olszak. We show that the local conformal factors are uniquely determined by the structure; consequently, every such manifold is globally conformal to a Sasakian manifold and its Lee form is exact. We then investigate the $k$-nullity condition $ R(X,Y)ξ=k\{η(Y)X-η(X)Y\}. $ We prove that a smooth nullity function is necessarily constant, including in dimension three. Moreover, the $k$-nullity condition is equivalent to the assertion that $f=\exp(σ)$ satisfies $ \mathrm{Hess}_g f=-(kf+C)g $ for a constant $C$, and hence to the fact that the conformal metrics $g$ and $g_0=\exp(-2σ)g$ have the same geodesic circles. We derive the range of the conformal factor, a local warped-product description, and a classification in the complete case: when the Lee form is nonzero, the complete metric is a simply connected space form of curvature $k$. Finally, we construct incomplete examples of nonconstant sectional curvature in every dimension $2n+1\geq 5$.

papers.title: Spacetime contactability in Galactic civilization networks: Contact counts and percolation
papers.abstract: The number of Galactic civilizations does not determine whether they are in contact. Allowing civilizations to appear at different times separates listening, audibility, mutual-listening, and relay networks, with a distinct reply-closing condition requiring a return signal within the sender's lifetime. For each network we derive the contact counts and estimate the connectivity threshold in a uniform population, then apply the results to a structured Galactic disc, separating the detection range $d_{\rm max}$ from the light horizon $cL$ through $χ=d_{\rm max}/cL$. The contactability is $η=πn d_{\rm max}^{2}$, where $n$ is the active civilization surface density. Averaged over civilization appearances, the lifetime listening count is $2η$ for all $χ$ and, at fixed detection range, for any lifetime distribution. Audibility and mutual-listening counts sum to $4η$, but connectivity depends on threshold behavior rather than counts alone. As $χ\rightarrow0$, the listening threshold decreases from the coeval value $4.51$ to $1.32\pm0.01$. Assuming an ideal complete survey, our own non-detection gives the reference bound $η(R_0)\le2.75$ at the Sun's Galactocentric radius. This benchmark lies above the listening, audibility and relay thresholds throughout the range studied. Unlike the coeval model, the spacetime model can satisfy both this benchmark and a local connectivity criterion, moving the local-contact frontier outward by $3.2$ kpc. Under the same benchmark, civilizations hear at most $5.5$ others on average, while the mean reply-closing count falls below unity for $χ\gtrsim1$. Contact may therefore be common even when completed replies remain rare.

papers.title: Using LLM Agents to Evaluate Prosocial Interventions on Social Media Platforms
papers.abstract: Social media platforms are a primary source of information for many users. Although research explores various interventions to promote prosocial content or demote harmful content on platforms, there are few systematic methods for evaluating competing intervention designs before conducting costly human-subject experiments. We develop a simulation-based evaluation pipeline built on the OASIS framework. We generate 13,835 LLM-based agents, each with a unique profile. Over 20 time steps, we expose them to real-world Twitter/X posts and let them comment, like, repost, or follow. We use those agents to systematically evaluate three interventions that increase exposure to verified news: adding content, upranking content, and celebrity source cues. All interventions significantly increase news engagement, with upranking news to prominent feed positions producing the largest effects. These effects hold across agents' gender, age, and education levels. We validate our injection treatment results against a comparable human-subject study and find strong directional alignment and similar dose-normalized efficiency. Our results suggest that LLM-based agent simulations can support early-stage evaluation of platform interventions before human-subject deployment, and upranking may be more effective than news volume or source.

papers.title: Confoundry: Spatial Causal Discovery and Dynamic Effect Mapping from Earth Observation Time Series
papers.abstract: Earth observation time series provide extensive historical observations of environmental change, but causal relationships inferred from them may vary geographically and depend heavily on local model adequacy. We introduce Confoundry, a framework for spatially resolved causal discovery and dynamic effect estimation from heterogeneous Earth observation time series. Confoundry aligns multi-source raster data, removes deterministic seasonal and long-term variation, fits separate structural VAR--LiNGAM models at individual grid cells, and propagates bootstrap estimation uncertainty into mapped dynamic responses. Model diagnostics are evaluated spatially so that mapped responses can be restricted to locations meeting predefined model checks. We demonstrate the approach using monthly MODIS NDVI and ERA5-Land hydroclimatic variables over the Iberian Peninsula from 2005--2024. Of 27,050 fitted pixel models, 14,657 passed the primary diagnostic criteria. The retained models yield geographically heterogeneous model-implied NDVI responses to precipitation, temperature, potential evaporation, and shallow and deep soil moisture. Aggregated responses vary systematically along an external aridity gradient: water-related responses become relatively stronger toward drier environments, whereas temperature responses increase toward wetter conditions. A single-pixel synthetic benchmark illustrates substantial finite-record variation in recovered causal structure and dynamic effects from 20-year monthly time series. The results demonstrate that spatial causal mapping of Earth observation data is most informative when estimated responses, uncertainty, and local model adequacy are reported together.

papers.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings. (i) In the mean-field description the oscillations are born at a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and require a predominantly two-stage contagion (first-contact adoption probability $Q\lesssim0.17$) and a slow turnover; spontaneous activation acts as a perturbation that destroys them. (ii) In finite populations demographic noise sustains quasi-cycles also outside this region, with a spectrum and variance predicted by a linear noise approximation away from the Hopf bifurcation. (iii) Reducing the connectivity of the network damps the oscillation, because naive nodes see fewer active neighbours than in a well-mixed population, and correlations measured in simulations confirm this damping mechanism; a pair approximation predicts that the sustained cycle disappears below a critical mean degree $\kc$, which decreases as $Q$ and the turnover rate decrease, and a finite-size test with up to $3.2\times10^5$ nodes confirms this threshold in simulations. (iv) At low connectivity the amplitude no longer depends on $Q$, so that sparsity erases the signature of the two-stage mechanism, whereas a faster turnover reduces the relative amplitude at every connectivity. The irregular dynamics observed in simulations are noise-driven quasi-cycles, not chaos.

papers.title: A domain-specific atomistic model for Earth's core materials
papers.abstract: Understanding Earth's core requires accurate descriptions of multicomponent iron alloys under extreme conditions. Here, we develop the Earth's Core Atomistic Model (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys through sampling with a foundational atomistic model, targeted ab initio simulations, and iterative exploration. A compact dataset selected from nearly half a million configurations is consistently labeled using high-accuracy first-principles calculations and used to train a lightweight model. The model explicitly includes thermal electronic contributions and runs nearly two orders of magnitude faster than the original foundational model. ECAM corrects artifacts in the foundational model's description of core materials and reproduces the density, seismic velocity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams of Fe and binary alloys in agreement with previous ab initio calculations. ECAM is expected to enable more realistic modeling of chemical partitioning and crystallization in Earth's core. Our workflow also provides a practical route from foundational-model sampling to efficient domain-specific simulation.

papers.title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
papers.abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. We formalize this effect with support-identifiability rate (SIR), construct support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluate a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals. On filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 train/dev/test steps), the original protocol has SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows and a support-only rule reaches 1.0000 OOV Exact@1. Support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; the strongest conditional reranker obtains 0.7214 overall Exact@1, 0.7988 on IV rows, and 0.5668 on OOV rows. The target-free dual-path system reaches Proposal Recall@16 0.6915 and end-to-end Exact@1 0.5212, compared with oracle conditional Exact@1 0.7450. On Mind2Web, the same audit yields SIR 0.2380 and an oracle-to-proposal gap of 0.2125. A 200-row semantic audit labels 0.7150 of exact-key OOV targets as semantically novel, 0.2450 as locator/string variation, and 0.0400 as ambiguous (Cohen's $κ=0.8173$). These measurements show why support composition must be controlled alongside candidate accuracy when offline results are used to reason about deployment.

papers.title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
papers.abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.

papers.title: One Rater to Score Them All: Frozen Large Language Model Anchoring for Video Quality of Experience
papers.abstract: Quality of Experience results for video streaming cannot be compared across studies, because public databases share neither test material nor subjects. This work introduces a common reference rater: an open-weights large language models with a fixed rubric and greedy decoding that scores the delivery events of every session and supplies the shared items that score equating requires. The rater is used without training, and it reads only the playback event log of startup delay, stalls and quality switches, which most delivery databases retain even when they share nothing else. A monotonic curve then maps each study's native scale onto the common scale. On 3{,}552 sessions from four studies covering four rating scales, the rater attains a Spearman correlation of 0.809 on VL04 of the ITU-T P.1203 collection, exceeding P.1203 mode~0 on the same sessions, with a Krippendorff alpha of 0.974 over repeated scoring and 0.951 across three serving providers. Sessions from three further laboratories give correlations from 0.756 to 0.787. After calibration, the four studies are placed on a single 0 to 100 scale with a held-out error between 7.8 and 13.3 points, and a mean VMAF of 60 corresponds to positions 17 points apart in two of the studies.

papers.title: PyOTIS: an open-source Python package for stream solute transport with transient storage
papers.abstract: OTIS and OTIS-P provide transient-storage transport and parameter estimation, whereas E-OTIS adds coupled water-quality reactions in a separate MATLAB implementation. PyOTIS brings these workflows into an open-source Python package with legacy OTIS input support. Its contribution is software integration: a scriptable interface, structured simulation outputs, Jacobian-based parameter uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and selectable transport schemes. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) provides example loading, custom parameter entry, breakthrough-curve and storage-zone plots, reference overlays, and calibration of supplied cases with confidence intervals. The package retains the OTIS Crank--Nicolson formulation and the E-OTIS reaction network; these are inherited model components rather than new process formulations. Evaluation distinguishes code comparisons, analytical convergence, and fits to observations. For the six OTIS manual examples, the comparisons distinguish model outputs from field observations and include agreement to seven significant figures for the steady-state iron profile. The nine-species E-OTIS comparison reports maximum absolute differences of order $10^{-14}$\,mg\,L$^{-1}$ against MATLAB. The conservative analytical benchmark shows approximately second-order convergence. For Clackamas River calibration, residual sums of squares differ from OTIS-P by 3.65--5.12\%, although individual parameter estimates differ by up to 39.1\%. These results support implementation consistency for the tested cases without establishing unique parameter estimates or validating every reaction pathway. Source code, example inputs, and verification scripts accompany the package.

papers.title: Trace element distribution in coarse-grained Ca-Al-rich inclusions by femtosecond LA-ICP-MS: Implications for U-Pb chronology
authors: Elishevah M. M. E. van Kooten
papers.abstract: Calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) in chondrites are the first solids that formed in the Solar System, as established by U-Pb chronology. After initial condensation, coarse-grained CAIs experienced melting, resulting in igneous partitioning and spatial redistribution of trace elements among constituent minerals. Understanding these distributions is essential for identifying trace-element host phases and interpreting U-Pb ages. Rare earth elements (REEs) and the actinides Th and U are particularly informative tracers, yet actinide behavior in coarse-grained CAIs remains poorly constrained. Here, we present major- and trace-element distribution maps of six coarse-grained CAIs from CV3 (Vigarano-type) chondrites acquired by femtosecond laser ablation ICP-MS. In CAIs lacking perovskite or hibonite, our results show that Al,Ti-pyroxene is the dominant host of U, Th, and most REEs, with strong enrichments observed toward pyroxene grain edges, whereas light REEs reside in melilite. Trace-element zonation reflects igneous fractional crystallization and is overprinted by melt evaporation, which caused depletion of the most volatile REEs (Yb, Eu, Ce) and U in CAI outer regions and rims. Using Nd and Th distribution maps as proxies for Cm, we model the effects of 247Cm-235U decay on mineral-scale U isotopic compositions. Variable Cm-U partitioning among coexisting minerals is predicted to generate resolvable inter-mineral 235U/238U variations, with the largest excesses in melilite. These variations can produce apparent U-Pb age offsets of ~0.1-1.0 Myr when U isotopic compositions and radiogenic Pb are derived from isotopically distinct mineral reservoirs, but generally remain small (< 0.15 Myr) when using bulk U isotopic compositions. Our results demonstrate that fractional crystallization and melt evaporation exert a primary control on U distribution and isotope systematics in igneous CAIs.

papers.title: Möbius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection
papers.abstract: Multimodal humor detection requires interpreting language, vocal delivery, and visual behavior jointly. Expressive fusion must also regulate how interactions of different orders enter the final judgment. We propose Möbius Interaction Filtering (MoIF), which learns a modality-subset prediction function and imposes order-selective spectral regularization through its aggregation structure. Private temporal encoders and balanced reciprocal interaction construct supervised unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal predictors. Their uniform aggregate is exactly a Möbius-domain filter with a geometrically decreasing interaction-order response. This formulation retains higher-order representations while regulating their contribution to prediction. Controlled UR-FUNNY perturbations reveal a pronounced decline in label-aligned signal-to-noise ratio across interaction orders. The induced filter improves the final ratio by 1.62-2.79 times relative to the co-trained trimodal predictor while preserving its own clean class-aligned signal under perturbation. Five-seed experiments achieve 70.6% accuracy and weighted F1 on UR-FUNNY, exceeding thirteen reproduced methods on these detection metrics. CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI evaluations establish applicability to sentiment prediction, and cross-seed analyses show more stable estimates on all three datasets. MoIF connects the organization of multimodal interactions to their statistical reliability through an executable spectral constraint. Code is available at https://github.com/D-ST-Sword/MoIF.

papers.title: Large-area Spatially Aligned Anchors
papers.abstract: Extended Reality (XR) technologies, including Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR), offer immersive experiences merging digital content with the real world. Achieving precise spatial tracking over large areas is a critical challenge in XR development. This paper addresses the drift issue, caused by small errors accumulating over time leading to a discrepancy between the real and virtual worlds. Tackling this issue is crucial for co-located XR experiences where virtual and physical elements interact seamlessly. Building upon the locally accurate spatial anchors, we propose a solution that extends this accuracy to larger areas by exploiting an external, drift-corrected tracking method as a ground truth. During the preparation stage, anchors are placed inside the headset and inside the external tracking method simultaneously, yielding 3D-3D correspondences. Both anchor clouds, and thus tracking methods, are aligned using a suitable cloud registration method during the operational stage. Our method enhances user comfort and mobility by leveraging the headset's built-in tracking capabilities during the operational stage, allowing standalone functionality. Additionally, this method can be used with any XR headset that supports spatial anchors and with any drift-free external tracking method. Empirical evaluation demonstrates the system's effectiveness in aligning virtual content with the real world and expanding the accurate tracking area. In addition, the alignment is evaluated by comparing the camera poses of both tracking methods. This approach may benefit a wide range of industries and applications, including manufacturing and construction, education, and entertainment.

papers.title: Uncovering the Blind Spots of OKS-mAP: A Unified Protocol for Occlusion, Joint-Angle, and Temporal Evaluation of 2D Pose Estimators
papers.abstract: The dominant metric for 2D human pose estimation, OKS-mAP, has three blind spots: it does not distinguish visible from occluded keypoints, does not measure joint-angle error, and is silent on the temporal stability of tracking-free per-frame inference. We propose a supplementary protocol with three modules: (M1) OKS-mAP stratified by ground-truth visibility, with Delta_occ = mAP(v=1) - mAP(full), quantifying how much the aggregate metric masks occlusion-specific differences; (M2) joint-angle error (RMSE/MAE/P95) plus knee-valgus detection consistency; (M3) frame-to-frame displacement, median-filter residual jitter, and jump rate, before and after OneEuro smoothing. We ran it on four datasets (COCO val2017, CrowdPose, OCHuman, PoseTrack18) and four models from two architecture families (YOLO11s-pose, an occlusion-domain fine-tuned variant, ViTPose-B/L), under a common detector-free oracle protocol and an open-source harness. Delta_occ is negative in every combination (-0.19 to -0.47): aggregate mAP overestimates occluded-scene performance in every tested combination. Joint-angle error is amplified in occluded layers; angle metrics reveal differences mAP cannot localize, e.g., the smaller occlusion-trained model significantly outperforming a larger transformer in occluded elbows. On PoseTrack18 val, raw jitter matched between the two YOLO models; pixel-domain OneEuro smoothing cut jump rates 9-10% at no matched-scope AP cost; residual jitter persists after detector removal; the transformer pair's jump rate is significantly lower; smoothing benefits replicate across architectures. Stratified mAP tracks full mAP closely (sign-consistency 1.0, 12/12), serving magnitude diagnosis rather than re-ranking; angle-metric difference vectors (especially knee) partially diverge, suggesting independent information. The protocol and harness are open-sourced, complementing rather than replacing OKS-mAP.

papers.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Predict Atomic Oxygen Erosion of Polymers in Low Earth Orbit
papers.abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO), home to most active satellites, is projected to undergo a debris-fragmentation cascade known as Kessler Syndrome. In light of this eventuality, it is imperative to maximize the operational lifetime of LEO satellites. Instrumental to this goal is the development of next-generation polymeric materials with improved resistance to atomic oxygen (AO) erosion. Because genuine LEO exposure experiments are prohibitively expensive and LEO conditions are difficult to reproduce in the laboratory, data-driven approaches offer a promising alternative for accelerating materials discovery. Here, we develop a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) based on OpenAI's GPT-4o to predict the AO erosion yield ($E_y$) of polymers using a curated dataset of 201 measurements compiled from multiple NASA LEO exposure missions. The model achieves an order of magnitude error (OME) of 0.154 and a log-scaled coefficient of determination (log-$R^2$) of 0.719, outperforming conventional machine learning approaches while eliminating the need for extensive feature engineering. Notably, incorporating macroscopic descriptors such as film thickness and layering did not improve predictive performance, suggesting that AO erosion is governed primarily by chemical and environmental variables rather than bulk structural characteristics. This finding underscores the importance of chemically informed polymer design in developing materials with improved AO resistance, while demonstrating the ability of modern LLMs to effectively extract chemically meaningful relationships even when data is limited. Beyond its predictive accuracy, the proposed framework provides a scalable platform for rapidly screening candidate polymers, reducing reliance on costly spaceflight experiments.

papers.title: Landfalling tropical cyclones perturb Earth's rotation
papers.abstract: Natural disasters that devastate human societies can also alter Earth's rotation. The 2011 $M_w$ 9.1 Tōhoku earthquake, one of the most powerful earthquakes ever recorded, shortened the day by 1.80 microseconds. Tropical cyclones are the costliest weather disasters, yet whether they can alter Earth's rotation remains unknown. Here we use atmospheric reanalysis to estimate, and numerical simulations to confirm, that a landfalling tropical cyclone can transiently alter the length of day by amounts rivalling those by great earthquakes. For example, Hurricanes Harvey (2017) and Katrina (2005) lengthened the day by 1.87 microseconds and 2.29 microseconds, respectively. As the climate warms, tropical cyclones may become an increasingly important source of variability in Earth's rotation.

papers.title: Generative Learning on Manifolds for Probabilistic Seismic Performance Assessment and Structural Identifiability
papers.abstract: Seismic performance assessment relies on computationally expensive nonlinear simulations, limiting uncertainty quantification and inference of structural properties from observed responses. We develop a manifold-based generative framework that learns the joint distribution of uncertain structural parameters and seismic-response trajectories from limited high-fidelity simulations. Combining Diffusion Maps, score-based Diffusion Modeling, and Geometric Harmonics, the framework enables both forward probabilistic prediction and inverse inference. Applied to a nine-story steel moment-resisting frame, the results reveal which structural properties are identifiable from seismic performance and how uncertainty in these properties influences response. In particular, the learned representation captures post-capping degradation characteristics more effectively than individual strength parameters. Inverse inference identifies distinct structural configurations that produce similar seismic performance, with representative solutions independently validated using nonlinear simulations. These findings demonstrate how generative learning can support uncertainty-aware seismic assessment while revealing structural non-identifiability and alternative mechanisms underlying observed performance

papers.title: 51 Additions per Recursive Step for Rank-23 $3\times3$ Matrix Multiplication, Machine-Checked over Arbitrary Rings
papers.abstract: We present a rank-23 bilinear scheme for $3\times3$ matrix multiplication that uses 51 additions per recursive step in the alternative-basis (Karstadt-Schwartz) cost model, one below Nielsen's 52 (arXiv:2609.06588). The count 51 itself was first posted, on a different scheme, by Stapleton and Perminov (arXiv:2609.32388), found by heuristic sparse-basis search; the present work is independent and complementary: exactness and breadth rather than a single construction. The scheme is valid over every ring, so it recurses on block matrices, and its correctness is machine-checked in Lean 4/Mathlib. The count is exactly optimal for the scheme's equivalence class: we introduce an exact free-basis minimization procedure whose negative answers are exhaustion proofs, and use it to show that 51 is the minimum for this class, that 52 is exactly optimal both for Nielsen's class and for the class of the current flat-model record, and to sweep the complete Heule-Kauers-Seidl database of rank-23 classes. The sweep is complete: exactly four classes attain 51, all in a single HKS invariant family. We machine-check Stapleton and Perminov's scheme as well, and prove in Lean that their 51 is optimal for its class. Separately, we document a systematic gap between $\mathbb{F}_2$ and signed optima: the $\mathbb{F}_2$-optimal chains of a class typically admit no sign assignment under most of the class's integer sign models, and certificate lifting fails where a direct signed search succeeds.

papers.title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks proved easy for most models, others posed extreme challenges, and some yielded mixed results, with wide variations in performance. This clearly illustrates the need for benchmarks that address the limitations of the models in Brazilian Portuguese, allowing future training cycles to seek to overcome them. Project repository https://github.com/soberania-oficial/brasilidade

papers.title: Development of a Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Vector Optically Pumped Magnetometer Using a Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Vapor Cell and Direct Absorption Frequency Locking for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
papers.abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.

papers.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation tools are not publicly available, we first develop a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors, informed by data from a deployed AI clinical documentation product. Then, we develop a method for generating semi-synthetic clinician-edit data, informed by our taxonomy, on a discharge-summary generation task based on MIMIC-III, a public dataset. Finally, we introduce simple filtering methods for identifying actionable edits, with accuracy evaluated by expert review. We show empirically, on our semi-synthetic dataset, that naive fine-tuning on raw edited output increases ungrounded content, while our approach of progressively filtering toward grounded edits enables improvement on clinician-alignment metrics while retaining faithfulness to the input context.

papers.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
papers.abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. We also build SEL-Pairs, a benchmark of length-matched evidence and control deletions from three question-answering datasets. Quantitative and qualitative experiments with five reader models on it show that SELD consistently outperforms strong and recent baselines across compressors, compression rates and models, identifying the evidence-removing edit in 83% of matched pairs with unchanged answers, against 70% for the strongest baseline. These results show that evidence loss in compressed contexts can be detected even when the answer is unchanged.

papers.title: TimeOmni-o1: Bidirectionally Coupling Time Series Foundation Models and LLMs for Multimodal Reasoning and Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast well from large-scale pretraining but typically neither read nor generate text. Time series language models add a time series modality to the LLM but forecast on the LLM side, leaving the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability unused. We present TimeOmni-o1, which couples a pretrained TSFM and an LLM bidirectionally. In one direction, the TSFM encodes the series in compressed form for the LLM, which reasons over it together with the text. In the other, the LLM's reasoning is fed back into the TSFM, which produces the forecast conditioned on it. One model architecture thus reads and generates both series and text, reasons in text, and draws on the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability. To train it, we build MMTR, a multimodal time series reasoning dataset with annotated reasoning traces, covering both tasks across 12 domains with 500k+ samples. On MMTR, TimeOmni-o1 outperforms existing models on both understanding and forecasting across most domains, as well as the LLM and the TSFM inside it when used individually. The gains carry over to three open benchmarks, where it outperforms the dedicated time series models.

papers.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.

papers.title: From Relevant Posts to Attributable Spans: Explicit Symptom Evidence for Depression Questionnaire Inference
papers.abstract: Longitudinal social-media histories offer an opportunity to assess depression, potentially supporting the inference of standardized depression questionnaire responses. However, this task requires evidence that is semantically relevant to a symptom and attributable to the user, while being sufficiently specific to support an individual questionnaire item. Existing approaches rely on semantic similarity to retrieve posts, which can introduce misleading or non-attributable evidence, particularly in multi-symptom posts and discussions of others' experiences. We propose SREE (Symptom Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded InfErence), an evidence-grounded pipeline that extracts first-person and symptom-specific text spans, selects a representative subset using a Facility Location-inspired objective, and performs Evidence-Gated Inference over the selected evidence. We evaluate evidence retrieval on BDI-Sen and evidence-conditioned questionnaire inference on eRisk 2019-2021. Compared with state-of-the-art retrieval approaches, SREE achieves relative improvements of 70% in post-level precision and 59% in F1, while retaining at least 30% fewer posts. On multi-symptom sentences, it also outperforms dense retrieval in precision and F1 even with twice the retrieval budget. Across all three eRisk collections, SREE achieves the highest exact item-level agreement while remaining competitive on ordinal and aggregate metrics. These results highlight the importance of localizing attributable evidence and controlling its composition before inferring depression questionnaire responses.

papers.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
papers.abstract: Neural operators (NOs) have been introduced as deep learning-powered solutions to the computational bottleneck of solving families of problems. Once trained, an NO can rapidly output approximate solutions, avoiding the need to rerun classical solvers. However, standard NO architectures cannot guarantee static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces from market or model features and, as we verify experimentally, can yield negative PnL in downstream trading tasks. We introduce a certifiably arbitrage-free (AF) and universal encoder-decoder NO framework, continuously mapping inputs from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}$ over any fixed subset of $[0,\infty)^2$ to a convex combination of arbitrage-free European call-price surfaces by continuously solving an approximate nearest-neighbour problem. We show that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained predicted surface need not exist, implying that no-arbitrage cannot, in general, be restored through post-processing. Further, we show that standard NOs, such as the FNO and certain encoder-decoder NOs, admit parameter configurations whose outputs violate static no-arbitrage. Thus, out-of-the-box NOs generally cannot be certifiably restricted to arbitrage-free configurations, but may only be guided towards them through PINN-type regularization during training.

papers.title: Bayesian Retrieval of L-Band Absorption by Ice using SMOS Brightness Temperatures over the Antarctic Plateau
papers.abstract: The low absorption of microwaves at L-band in ice enables the retrieval of internal ice sheet parameters from satellite observations. However, knowing the precise value of the ice absorption $κ$a(T ) as a function of temperature is a strict prerequisite. The existing knowledge is well constrained above 2 GHz and under 200 MHz, lacking constraints in the P-and L-bands. In this study, we infer ice absorption values using the spatial variations of L-band radiometric observations across Antarctica and comparing them with internal ice temperature variations through a simple emission model. More importantly, we adopt a probabilistic approach to determine a credible interval for absorption, using a Bayesian retrieval method. Our algorithm seeks the optimal multiplier factor $α$ to apply to the current lowest estimate ice absorption formulation $κ$a(T ) proposed by M{ä}tzler 2006, and computes the probability distribution of $α$. The results show the absorption is most likely 1.5 to 1.7 times higher than this lowest formulation, which reduces the actual sensing depth at L-band.

papers.title: EoSAlign: An Open-Source Software for Calculating, Comparing, and Aligning Pressure Under Extreme Conditions
papers.abstract: Accurate pressure determination is essential in high pressure experiments. Inconsistencies among pressure scales limit direct comparisons and contribute to uncertainty in measured properties, such as, phase boundaries, melting conditions, and thermodynamic models, especially above 100 GPa where existing scales diverge by >10 GPa. EoSAlign, an open-source software, can calculate, compare, and align pressures using a range of published calibrations. EoSAlign calculates pressure from experimental measurements (such as volume (A^3), Raman shift (cm^-1), or luminescence peak position (nm)) and it can be used to compare pressure values from different pressure standards. Using EoSAlign, we fit and align the bridgmanite and post-perovskite equations of state to a common scale, enabling us to reduce pressure scale related differences. EoSAlign can be applied to any high pressure data analysis to compare experimental results, improve consistency between studies, and advance our understanding of planetary interiors and high pressure physics.

papers.title: Efficient Conversion of Algorithms to Linear Programs
papers.abstract: The expressiveness of Linear Programming (LP) has motivated research on an LP compiler that generates polynomial-size LPs for polynomial-time solvable problems, including those having exponential extension complexity. By automating modeling from high-level algorithmic descriptions, the compiler offers a promising alternative to algebraic modelling languages. However, the resulting LPs are extremely large, posing challenges for existing solvers. Recently, we have introduced two LP compiler optimizations, namely Hierarachical Synchronization Barriers (HSB) and Constraint Sharing (CS), that address this challenge by exploiting structural and similarity-based patterns derived from the source code and the design of compiler-generated LPs, beyond what conventional compiler and presolve techniques can achieve in isolation. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive evaluation of these optimization methods on fundamental combinatorial algorithms and introduce the Execution Domain Aware (EDA) optimization framework to address a limitation revealed by this analysis. The framework reinterprets structural synchronizations as a time abstraction layer within which other optimizations can target localized reductions while remaining agnostic to time-step transitions. Across a broad suite of benchmarks, HSB and CS consistently generate smaller LPs, achieving LP file-size reductions of up to 96% and 53%, respectively, while also improving numerical conditioning, solver performance, and solution quality. HSB provides the strongest and most robust overall gains. The EDA framework further broadens the range of benchmarks that can benefit from HSB when its underlying structural assumptions are less effective. We view this work as a step toward systematic generation of Compact Integer Programming formulations for problems with exponential-size Integer Programs having polynomial-time separation oracles.

papers.title: An Idealized Model of Buoyant Gas Spreading and Silt Release beneath Rough Cave Ceilings
papers.abstract: Gas exhaled by open-circuit divers collects under the ceilings of submerged caves, migrates along the rock, and dislodges loose silt that then falls through the passage, a process that cave divers call percolation. This study develops an idealized model of the process. Buoyant gas under a self-affine rough ceiling is treated as a quasi-static sequence of pools that fill to their spill points, release gas that climbs to the next high point, and merge where their levels meet. Moving contact lines strip silt from the rock, and the released silt settles as a spectrum of grain sizes that reduces the distance at which a diver can see. The computation agrees exactly with an independent depression-filling algorithm, conserves gas volume to round-off, and reproduces the known exponents of invasion percolation in its capillary limit. A balance between the relief of the ceiling and its dip defines a pool scale that organizes where gas collects, and the area covered by gas from a single source grows more slowly than the volume supplied, as predicted by the self-affine geometry. The cutoff at the pool scale is soft, so large pools persist on steeper ceilings than the scale alone would suggest. In a reference passage, the lead diver of a team releases far more silt than the diver behind, and a team releases far less than the sum of its members acting alone, because the lead diver fills the pools and strips the paths that later divers reuse. This ordering holds across every detachment efficiency and ceiling geometry tested. Visibility toward the exit at eye level continues to decline for an hour or more after a team has passed, as fine silt descends from a nearly opaque layer beneath the ceiling. Absolute silt masses and sighting ranges depend on quantities that have not been measured in caves, and the results are best read as scaling relations and comparisons between scenarios.

papers.title: D-TINs for Track-Sampled Ice Sheet Surface Reconstruction from Satellite Altimetry Data
papers.abstract: Satellite altimetry samples ice sheets densely along tracks but sparsely across tracks, with frequent gaps in spatial coverage. We study the impact of this irregular support on surface reconstruction and introduce a new method, D-TIN, that applies Delaunay triangulation and barycentric interpolation directly to observed locations. A spatial holdout removes contiguous track intervals and nearby same-pass observations. We compare D-TIN with two common workflows, kriging and tile-based polynomial interpolation, to evaluate its accuracy and computational efficiency. Across seven ICESat-1 campaigns, D-TIN reduces RMSE by 12.1 m to 23.6 m relative to independent 5 km tile and polynomial based reconstruction. Its aggregate accuracy is close to the ordinary kriging workflow using a 1 km grid on the commonly used GStatSim platform while its median runtime is 252 times lower. A fixed-weight multiscale extension of D-TIN, called MS-D-TIN, gives the lowest aggregate RMSE, 67.5 m, while retaining the low computational cost of the D-TIN family.

papers.title: First-passage tests of anomalous transport closures in heterogeneous aquifers
papers.abstract: Breakthrough curves (BTCs) record arrival times, but anomalous transport models are often fitted with time-normalized spatial concentration profiles. Here, the effect of this mismatch on groundwater-transport upscaling is tested. Analytical limits and high-$q$ scaling were verified first. Six first-passage models were then fitted to particle arrivals from 36 two-dimensional digital aquifer runs. The set included exact ADE, $q$ and time-memory extensions, a joint memory-$q$ model, Gamma-CTRW, and a two-path inverse-Gaussian mixture. After the operator was corrected, memory-qFPT was not selected in any run. AICc selected the two-path model in 20 runs, Gamma-CTRW in 15, and q-FPT in one. Median downstream holdout log-RMSE was 0.904, 0.914, and 0.959 for the two-path, Gamma-CTRW, and memory-qFPT models, respectively. The memory-$q$ parameters also failed an independent plume-scaling test ($R^2=0.189$; slope $=-0.332$). Meanwhile, multimodal downstream BTCs increased from 0\% in homogeneous media to 100\% in the strongest heterogeneity class. Gamma-CTRW was also favored in an independent synthetic field. Observation consistency is therefore necessary but not sufficient for physical validation. In these simulations, pathway and waiting-time structure was supported more strongly than a unique memory-$q$ law.

papers.title: Addendum and Corrigendum to: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
papers.abstract: In various special cases, we provide an alternative argument for equivalence between Kostant positivity of some involutions in type $A$ and the conjunction of the categorical Kåhrstr{ö}m's condition for these involutions with indecomposability of the images of the corresponding simple modules in category $\mathcal{O}$ under projective functors.

papers.title: Applicability of a Thermodynamic Model to Rich-Hydrogen Flammability Assessment in SMR Containments
papers.abstract: Hydrogen combustion remains a critical safety concern during severe accidents in small modular reactors (SMRs). The compact containment can develop rich-hydrogen atmospheres through zirconium oxidation while oxygen gradually accumulates via radiolysis. Conventional flammability assessment methodologies, however, have been validated and applied only for lean-hydrogen atmospheres. This study establishes a thermodynamic flammability assessment method for rich-hydrogen conditions using the Calculated Adiabatic Flame Temperature (CAFT). In rich mixtures the deficient reactant becomes oxygen and the Lewis number exceeds unity, matching the hydrocarbon regime where CAFT is established. The CAFT was evaluated at 21 points along the measured upper flammability limit boundary of the U.S. NRC FITS database. The limit temperature remains quasi-constant within 17% across steam fractions of 5-50%. Its minimum value of 1112.5 K was adopted as a conservative threshold. The criterion was applied to the NuScale severe accident scenario LCC-05T-03. A transient flammable window is identified during the 44-48 hour interval, when 8-10% oxygen coexists with vigorous hydrogen generation and low steam fractions. These results show that the oxygen criterion alone cannot resolve transient flammability windows. The CAFT criterion enables more comprehensive flammability assessment for SMR containments.

papers.title: Pooling ETAS triggering parameters across subduction margins: forecast transfer, estimator stability and sequence-limited skill in Mexico
papers.abstract: Pooling earthquake-triggering parameters can reduce estimation variability on margins with few recorded sequences, but its forecast value must be distinguished from the stability of simply freezing a fitted law. We fit the ETAS model to the Mexican national catalog above magnitude 5.0, using the Slab2 coverage mask as the domain. On a 4.7-year holdout the model gains 1.45 bits per earthquake over a time-independent spatial Poisson reference (cluster-resampled interval [-0.03, +2.75] bits), with two clusters carrying 90% of the signed gain. Using the Global CMT catalog we fit eight disjoint subduction margins and a joint model on 3,210 earthquakes sharing six triggering parameters with a background rate per margin; BIC favors the joint model by 184 units, though a parametric bootstrap rejects its exact shared specification. Transferred into Mexico with the local background fixed, six of seven foreign triggering sets score within 0.07 nats per event of the home fit. In leave-one-margin-out evaluation, the excluded-pool law's event-weighted paired gain is +0.0334 [+0.0002, +0.0670] nats per event; its lower limit sits barely above zero and crosses zero under alternative cluster-linking rules, so we read it as neither conclusive superiority nor guaranteed noninferiority. Across 28 overlapping annual evaluations, local refitting minus a pooled law frozen before the first origin has mean gain -2.07 nats/year (moving-block interval [-6.92, +1.15]), while local productivity varies by a factor of 5.4. Coverage of these intervals is unmeasured, and a measured analogue fell short of nominal; the paired median contrast's significance depends on a Gutenberg-Richter slope that is conventional rather than measured. These results support pooling as a regularized alternative to local fitting, short of equivalence, a universal law, or an optimal update policy.

papers.title: We Used It Anyway: Low Trust and High Adoption of Large Language Models in Requirements Engineering Education
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping how students approach Software Engineering activities, particularly those centered on textual artifacts. This paper reports on the experience of integrating a non-restrictive LLM use within a first-year Master's course in Software Engineering, in which students completed a semester-long Software Engineering project divided in a Requirements Engineering (RE) phase and a software testing phase. Following the completion of the RE phase of the project, we administered a 12-question survey to 43 students to investigate which LLM tools they used, for which activities, how they evaluated AI-generated outputs, and how they envisioned the role of LLMs in future SE curricula. Our findings show that LLM use was nearly universal among respondents and concentrated primarily on text-intensive activities such as use-case narratives, consistency checking, brainstorming, and refinement of existing artifacts. Despite this widespread adoption, most students perceived AI-generated outputs as inferior to their own work, frequently reporting issues related to incorrect or incomplete content, mismatches with course-specific conventions, over-engineering, and limitations in diagram generation. Nevertheless, students continued to rely extensively on LLM as a reviewer, critic, and productivity aid rather than as a fully autonomous artifact generator. We also observe that students' choice of models was strongly influenced by access to premium subscriptions available for free for student accounts, highlighting the role of economic accessibility in shaping educational AI ecosystems. The results suggest that the most significant challenge in the adoption of LLMs within Requirements Engineering education is not whether students use these tools, but whether they possess the skills required to critically evaluate, contextualize, and correct its outputs.

papers.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
papers.abstract: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded.
